pages.text: There's much theories surrounding the inhabitants of the $(l)fortresses$() within the Nether and their theoretical abilities in magic. Unfortunately, any texts holding such insights have all withered away like the inhabitants themselves.
However, perhaps some of the former inhabitants have a more studious grip on such knowledge, maybe blowing a $(l)special horn$() can call forth one of them.
You've been working on improving your Necromantic powers when you heard something. There's something within the Desert that can increase your knowledge, perhaps within those $(l)pyramids$()?
Whispers mentioned of spirited away knowledge being hidden in the sands.
You've heard of odd parchments found within the $(l)moss-covered structures$() within the $(l)Jungles$(), parchments that speak of some sort of magical rites.
These parchments are said to be found within $(l)jungle temples$()
Rumors abuzz of a powerful hammer that was a high-end $(l)Illager$() artisanship, holding the very storms within itself.
It's said that certain $(l)hammer-wielding illagers$() hold such a hammer, or perhaps a replica, that only shows its power when struck by $(l)lightning$().

You've pondered on the Ravagers and how the Illagers obtain them. Rumor has it that they're a result of the abhorrent dark magic. Perhaps the $(l)Woodland Mansions$() holds the answer to this question.
Search through $(l)Woodland Mansions$() for any information.
These Respawn Anchors hold the ability to bring the dead back to the Nether without Bedastrophic consequences. You begin to wonder what other abilities these blocks possess...
What happens if one were to use the anchor on a crypt lord's $(l)plundered jar$() or used $(l)crystal ball$() within their $(l)original locations$()?

From the warred scrolls there's mention of a powerful variant, stronger than even the Redstone Golems, that was made and banished to a lost land. There's also mentioned of how some scholars recorded how this beast was made before they were destroyed, but surely there's some that still remains...
The scroll mentions that the beast's design may have came from a being of $(l)The End$(), and its secrets lies within a $(l)terminal of power$().

Whispers of war-machines used in ancient times that possesses great power have reached your ears. They say that these beasts were made of rock and redstone and have been used within $(l)ancient$() structures to defend and attack.
They say that these monstrous machines were utilized in $(l)ancient cities$() and buried $(l)strongholds.$()

Travelers from all over have tales of coming across odd highly robed beings chanting towards a monolith made what appears to be obsidian. They mentioned that the area around them made them feel uneasy...

Rumors of old, rotting shacks have reached your ear. Apparently, old and powerful witches live within those decrepit dens, studying and brewing all kinds of dark magic. Yet when you come across these shacks, you spot no ancient witch, but a peculiar crystal ball... you wonder what will happen if you were to use it...
The desert is full of buried secrets, but these appeared to be once a site of a ritual, but of what?
A stinky plant has been spotted, or more likely scented, in the canopies of Jungles. They not only smell, and look pretty, but are said to also contain the energies of the Jungle.

You've heard of ancient crypts burrowed under the earth, warping the landscapes above its unholy structure. Rumor has it that these Crypts hold great treasures, forbidden secrets... and horrible monsters.
The Illagers are quite progressive compared to their passive cousins. Some have set up some Manors outside of their Mansions to study the world and its aspects.
Within the End, lies a structure that holds various treasures and secrets. It is rumored to be guarded by subspecies of Endermen, Enderlings.

Going through the structure, one can come across Void Keys and arenas containing Void Frames. Using said keys on the frames will summon forth a powerful creature, that drops a Void Shard when slain. The structure also contains vaults that can be opened with the keys.

On top of the terminal lies a Void Shrine. It requires four Void Shards to be inserted before a powerful warrior is summoned. Defeating the warrior will cause an object to appear, placed on the Void Shrine, that can give a monstrous secret.

Littered across the world, there have been sightings of haunted graveyards that are rumored to be cursed with dark magic and some reported to have heard growling around the area. Perhaps some of the graves holds some treasure...

Jades are one of the most illusive ores to find in the world. They hold the power of the winds within themselves and can only be found in places of high elevations like Mountains, specifically the peaks of them.
There are rumors that tribes of Illagers have set up blacksmiths high atop of mountains, one that may contain a treasure of the Illagers.

There were once holy monasteries that have been abandoned due to circumstances like being overrun by undead. Now these temples have been occupied by a sinister cult that wishes to perform an unholy ritual...
While Illagers tend to stick to one side of magic, there are rumors that some of them seek to master all of them and hold themselves into specialize keeps... along with some prisoners.
There had been legends and rumors about great trees that are hollowed and infested with spiders, and that they might've been planted atop of an old abandoned mine...
You've heard of nomads, traveling from the highest sanctum, setting up shrines to the very winds on the very peaks. Who knows what kinds of treasure are held within?

The closest followers of the first Nether Cultist, Apollyon, these terrific beings spread the word of the Great Flame alongside their master when they walked the Overworld. Some Apostles used to be Kings, Lords or Nobles, while others range from normal Villagers to the most ill-witted Nitwits. When the emissary appears, the water around them boils, and the sky darkens.

An Apostle doesn't deign to use their true power when confronted with a violent heathen. They would shoot arrows upon them, while occasionally shooting a Hell Blast or summoning fiendish servants to defend themselves. The fiend would teleport, leaving a cloud of smoke, when hit after a number of times or after casting a spell.

When lowered to half of their maximum health, the Apostle will regenerate their health and reveal their true might. When fought in the Overworld or dimensions similar to it, a storm will rain upon the world once they reveal themselves in their horrid form. Meteors will fall around them and the true battle begins. The Apostle will try to teleport more often, and their arrows are much potent in damage and effects.

Throughout the battle, they will cast horrid spells upon their target, from a rain of lava to hurling souls damned to the fires of Nether towards their foe. If their target was close to them, the Apostle will summon a circle of fire that after a short time, burst causing whatever creature near them to be knocked into the sky. The bursts and the flaming tornado curses the target with Burn Hex, which prevents Fire Resistance from working.

The Apostle regenerates health once their arrows pierce their victims. However, when struck with a weapon enchanted with Smite, they won't be able to regenerate their health for a time depending on the level of the Enchantment.

The blood of an Apostle courses with Necrotic and Nether Energies. With it, one can either cheat death or create miracles. It appears that an Apostle doesn't possess too much blood and only by slaying them can a sizeable amount be extracted. When slain, the storm will ebb and the meteors will stop falling.
Infernos are cousins to the blazes, but are enchanted to be undeterred by simple water and their flames burns even those that are immune to fire.

Smaller but far superior to ghasts, these agonized monsters belch out balls of unholy flames that burns through all. Occasionally, these creatures would shoot out a regular lavaball, that can be swung back at them.
There are whispers that their blood remains Pure when dropped within the Nether...
Gigantic spiders that attacks those who dare mess with their dens, with fangs that poison even the undead.
These creatures will try to directly attack their target, but if their children were to join the fight they would instead circle around them, letting their kids have their meal.

Long dead officials risen to undeath to maintain and guard the Crypt with their undead servants. They appear to be an offshoot of the ancient Necromancers of the desert, utilizing the power of the cold.
Summons multiple Strays and shoots Ice Spikes.
pages.name: Cairn Necromancer

pages.text: Older and wiser, yet still malicious, Witches that have created and utilize far greater brews than their lesser kin. Their Hats are said to help make extra witch brews.
Deals damage when getting hit.
pages.name: Crone

pages.text: The hat of a Crone is a powerful object that when worn, gives a 25%% chance of not using up a Potion, and a 10%% chance of not using up a Brew. It also gives a chance of bottling, up to three extra brews if the wearer dons a Witch Robe, instead of two if the wearer had been don a regular Witch Hat instead.
The Crypts hold potent necrotic energies that it occasionally spawns slimes made out of bones and ectoplasm.
Their attacks inflicts the Sapped effect.
pages.name: Crypt Slime

pages.text: A powerful entity of The End, called to guard the secrets of the dimension and the void.

The being holds mastery over both swordsmanship and void magic, piercing their enormous blade through their foes and summoning orbs of void magic that shoots towards their targets. Their blade and attacks inflicts Void Touched.

It's best to stay clear of the Ender Keeper, through using mobility spells such as $(l:goety:focuses/wind/launch_focus)Launch$() or $(l:goety:focuses/wild/grapple_focus)Grapple$() to move away. Be vigilant when calling upon Servants to face this foe, for one of its attacks will drag nearby creatures towards itself, absorbing their health, before letting loose an explosion of void.
When slain, the shrine from which they are called from will reveal its treasure, a mysterious blueprint... one that with the help of dark magic will reveal its contents.
The Keeper also drops some echoes of the very void itself, which can be used to create powerful spells and items.
Consisting of varied subspecies of Enderman, these odd creatures appear to defend something from the End, and are more hostile than their main counterpart.

While they share many traits, such as vulnerability to water, they appear to be more tolerant towards Endermites, and teleport less frequently. Some might disappear for a time after teleporting, before reappearing to confuse their foes.
Unfortunately, the book is incapable of showing their eyes properly for some arcane reason.
pages.name: Watchling

pages.text: Accounted as being the creepiest looking, Watchlings are noted to prefer defending their home in simple ways, namely smashing and swinging at their foes with their big arms.

The most resilient of Enderlings, these fiery entities shoot volleys of hot goo at their foes, though if a foe gets close to them or get hurt by them, they would stop their attack and temporarily run or teleport away.

Similar to Web Spiders, these creatures will attempt to trap their foes in their web-like goop before attacking them with their pinwheel like arms. Unlike their brethren, these strange beings won't disappear for a time when teleporting, preferring to teleport away in an instant.
These entities' strength surpasses most creatures you have encountered, as their hammer like arms are not to be trifled with.
Most recounting of them seems to have them guard something, whether it be an object or an area. It appears they gain strength and abilities when bonded with an Eye of Ender.
Not only will an Enchanted Endersent drop its eye, but will also drop a Void Shard, which can be used on a Void Shrine.

While you were busy with your day, you seemed to be attacked by a lone Illager that seemed to be an Evoker. Unlike other Evokers, this one seems to be far more powerful and seems to be using their Totem to the fullest.

It seems the Illagers despised how you've managed to delve into secrets that they believed belonged to them. You feel that this Evoker was simply one that was too enraged by how quickly you've discovered said secrets. You have a feeling that the more you delve into the dark arts, the more Illagers will take umbrage.

The guardians and sentries of the Crypts, no doubt brought to life through Necroturgic magic. Due to their nature as unholy constructs, they are immune to almost all Debuffs and won't burn in flames. They will, however, still melt in lava and take more damage from Smite.
Their Shields can be disabled through Axe.
pages.name: Haunted Armor

pages.text: The blade held by the Haunted Armors have a special property where they have a chance of halving a creature's armor points. They can be repaired using Cursed Metal Ingots on an Anvil
pages.title: Fell Blade

pages.text: The armor seems to be more or less an ornate Cursed Metal version of regular Iron Armor, with two exceptions. One, it provides small amount of toughness. Two, wearing the full set of armor gives an additional 4 armor points.
pages.title: Cursed Knight Armor

pages.text: These unholy priests leads a congregation of those who worshipped the Great Flame. They're knowledge over the dark realm grants them hellish abilities.

Upon death, they drop their antlered bone helmet that provides some benefits upon the wearer, so long as it's not broken. One of which includes causing newly converted Heretics and Mavericks to serve you. Another is causing Witches, Warlocks, Reprobates, and other Cultists to be neutral to the wearer. It can also be repaired using Bones. Due to its size, it cannot be worn as a Curio.
A cousin to Witches, these partisans shout unholy chants at their targets, summoning flame blasts beneath their feet, summon forth a creature of the Nether from a dying breath of a nearby creature.
They're resistant to magic much like their Witch cousins.
pages.name: Heretic

pages.text: If a Villager sleeps near an active Nether Portal, they have a chance of transforming into a Heretic.
More hands on than their cousins, they apply potions effects through their blades, before fleeing and drinking a potion to buff themselves.
They're resistant to magic much like their Witch cousins.
pages.name: Maverick

pages.text: If a Wandering Trader is underneath a Crying Obsidian Block, they have a chance of transforming into a Maverick.

Illagers higher in rank and prestige than Evokers. Indeed, they are most likely to be the leader of the Illager tribe they are a part of. Ministers are notorious for plundering civilizations and their oratory skills, which they use to empower other Illagers or to viciously mock their foes.

It is said that the Staff they wield is either inspired by or plundered and modified from a nameless kingdom, with the staff's orb radiating great magic. Ministers are also good at blocking hits with their staff, though unfortunately for them, their staffs aren't as durable as a standard shield.
pages.title: Minister's Staff

pages.text: Perhaps there's a way to plunder the staff, or at the very least, its orb, without shattering it, though at least you can potentially remake it with the leftovers.
Hooded apparitions that are proficient at wielding scythes with a hunger for souls.
Reapers have a chance of dropping Grave Dusts, which are useful for crafting certain necromantic objects.
pages.title: Grave Dust

pages.text: Unlike Witches, these heathens throw an entire cask of potions that all mixed into an acidic pool. They are said to also deliver these potions to dark forces.
They're resistant to magic much like their Witch cousins.
pages.name: Reprobate

pages.text: If a Wandering Trader gets struck by lightning, they will transform into a Reprobate.
It seems there are more ways for piles of bones to manifest their ire.

These shambling undead shoot arrows that causes the victim to go into Spasms. They seem to appear only in thunderstorms, exposed to the skies, or when a, non-Wither, Skeleton is struck by a lightning bolt. They take half the amount of damage from shock or lightning attacks.

Desecrating and trying to open a jar of the grand tomb unleashed an enraged lord that once ruled the structure. It appears that they hold a piece of dark magic with them that they couldn't complete within their lifetime.

Unfortunately for would be treasure hunters and mages, the dark master of the Crypt managed to stay bound to the material world to guard their treasure. Their heads are the source of their power and intellect and is protected whenever they reconstituted their armored yet skeletonized bodies.

During the battle, they appear to be wielding a special blade that's similar to the Haunted Armor's Fell Blade, but far more chilling, to the point that simple cut from it can cause rapid freezing. They can be repaired using Cursed Metal Ingots on an Anvil
pages.title: Frozen Blade

pages.text: A far more ornate and upgraded version of the Cursed Knight Armor, providing more armor and toughness.
pages.title: Cursed Paladin Armor

pages.text: After killing a bunch of Illagers that have come to slay you for stealing their knowledge, you've managed to document the ones that you've never encountered before.

Most of these Illagers seemed to only go after those who had discovered or stolen their secrets as they aren't found stationed in Woodland Mansions or Outposts, and they seemed to only partake in Raids if those discoverers are within that village. What's certain is that these brand of Illagers are high ranking enough to bring even Ravagers in their pursuit.
A powerful and well-read Evoker that seems to be using an odd Ruby Shard on their heads to power up their magics. Their Totem was either gifted or taken from others.
Looks to be the result of an experiment between a Vex and a Vindicator, these beings remain invisible when they're not charging at their target.

All round practitioners of the dark arts, these mages aren't specialized on one element like the other illager spellcasters, making them more unpredictable than the rest. Highly trained sorcerers tend to gild their robes with precious materials.
Greater than the average Pillagers, lesser but more reaching than Vindicators, these disciplined foot-soldiers might've been inspired by the scrolls of the desert.

Wolves and dogs tamed and bred by Illagers for the purpose of chasing down queries or mauling their enemies in advance of their troops. They can come in different sizes with different stats, and rarely have reinforcements appear nearby.
Violent steeds of the Illagers, rumored to be made from the weakest of their kind or as a punishment, that charges at their targets with or without a rider.

Blacksmiths and warriors, these Illagers tend to either be forging away from plain sight, or dispatch on certain areas. They say that some of their hammers are made to absorb and control the lightning itself.
Some believe them to be former Geomancers or Wind Callers that decided to harness the power of lightning itself. They seek out the tallest sanctum to plunder its secrets.
Kin to the Iceologers, these criers have more tricks up their sleeves than their mono-spelled cousins. The Illagers believe that they're crying out of admiration of the cold.
Like Enchanters, Preachers are a rare type of Illager that work to support their brethren rather than fighting head on. These Illagers will follow and heal any nearby injured raider.
Disease-ridden aristocrats that spread civilization-ending pestilence to foreigners. Fortunately, they prefer to shoot from afar than go into barbaric melee.
An unexpected Illager trained to attack magic users as they're immune to their spells. They wield flaming swords and throw Harming Potions.
You've noticed that some strange spiders have been appearing around lately, whether in certain areas or in general darkness like other monsters.

Spiders that produces more webs than other variants, these cowardly arachnids will shoot their webs at their target, only attacking when caught. If their target goes near them, the spider will attempt to flee. Their constant web production causes them to drop intact Cobwebs.
Spiders that appear in cold biomes, their bites gives Slowness much like a Stray's arrow. They can walk on and are immune to Powder Snow.
Appearing in Crypts, these bone covered arachnids shoot Bone Shards from afar and will attack with their bites if their target is near.
One of the highest ranking of all Illagers, the Viziers seems to possess a powerful ruby that amplifies spells and magic.

In battle, they charge upon their target with an Iron Sword multiple times before summoning Fangs upon their feet. When injured, an Irk will be summoned to defend their master, a ranged cousin of the Vex.
Once injured enough, or there are lot of Irks around them, the Vizier will cast a spell that would siphon the life force of all surrounding Irks, healing them in the process.
When slain, their killer will be struck with Bad Omen at it's highest level. There are rumors that the Viziers would grant shards of their mighty ruby to certain Evokers.
pages.title: Ruby of Souls

pages.text: Cousins to Witches, Warlocks are hostile creatures that attack by summoning Wartlings upon their foes. If their target gets close to them, they will throw a bunch of Snap Fungi in the air where they might hit said target.
They're resistant to magic much like their Witch cousins.
pages.name: Warlock

pages.text: If a Villager is underneath a Crying Obsidian Block, they have a chance of transforming into a Warlock.
A strange entity that appears near beings that have a high amount of soul energy.
When slain, they drop some odd 'essences' that seems to suck in light. Perhaps they can be used to create certain items.
pages.title: Essence of Shadow

pages.text: Some, who have seen and survived an encounter of one, believed them to be a creation of a $(l:world/crypts)dark and cold place$()...

In ancient times, these necromancers were overseers of the Nether Fortresses, wielding great magical powers. Unfortunately, when the Blazes turned against their masters, turning the living inhabitants into charred withered remains, the necromancers, for all their power, were put down through either numbers and aid from what were referred to as 'Wildfires'... and perhaps even from the Piglins.

Unlike in life, these necromancers are immune to flame and still hold great power. Their flaming pillars that either surrounds them or their target burn even on fire-resistant foes, and they would frequently summon Wither Skeletons to aid it. Fortunately for you and other dark wizards, these necromancers still held upon their, admittedly decayed and withered, manuscripts that holds some knowledge of their magical practices.
Much like regular Wither Skeletons, their hatred for Piglins burn hot even in death.
Mysterious shades that summon flames upon their target's feet that, rather being hot, freezes the soul. They also have the ability to teleport but only do so if their target is near them.
Despite their fiery powers, they are not immune to fire.
pages.name: Wraith

pages.text: Wraiths have a chance of dropping an Ectoplasm. The Ectoplasm is useful for crafting Necroturgic artifacts and spells.
pages.title: Ectoplasm

pages.text: A variant of the wraith, one that rather than summon freezing flames, summon clouds of acidic gas upon their foes.

A variant of the wraith, these phantasms lack the ability to teleport and summon less Ice Bouquets than their cousin. However, they have the power to breath their icy flames upon their target, if said target goes close to them.
More types of zombies have been sighted lately, with some appearing on certain areas or conditions.

These burnt corpses appeared to be remains of those struck by lightning, whose attacks leave their victims in fits of Spasms. They seem to appear only in thunderstorms, exposed to the skies, or when a Zombie is hit by a lightning bolt. They also take half the damage amount from shock or lightning attacks.

Having a Wraith properly possess a Black Wolf results in a powerful, and unnatural, creature that can rend your enemies asunder through it's withering claws and curses or, if their foe is beyond their reach, summoning apparitions of their heads to bite them.

The beast can be healed by feeding it meat much like tamed wolves, and can passively heal if their owner dons a Wild Robe. Right-clicking on them with a Taglock Kit, that has a Tagged creature on it, will cause them to hunt said creature down before returning to their owner once they slay their query.
Upon death, the beast would be reduced to a soul where it can be right-clicked on a Black Wolf, loyal or not, to have it possess and mutate it back to its original form.
Mob based on 'Nightmare Stalker' from 'Born In Chaos' mod by 'mongoose_artist'.
With some reagents and dark magic, you've managed to transform a spider into a dreadful Brood Mother.

Not only are Brood Mothers make for powerful ride-able steeds, but they can shoot multiple web shots and lay spider eggs that will hatch into loyal spider servants. The resulting servant will spawn in different varieties depending on where it's egg is.
The arachnid can be healed by feeding it meat much like other spider servants, and can passively heal if their owner dons a Wild Robe.

You've discovered a more powerful variant of regular Necromancers, one that still retains their flesh and holds great power over the ocean, shooting torrents of steam missiles and conjure falling tridents around themselves. Rather than Skeletons, the ritual is performed on a Drowned instead.

Much like regular Necromancers, they can be taught to summon more than just Drowned. Right-clicking with certain Necromancy Focuses allows them to summon more types of servants. Right-clicking on them with an empty hand will cause the Necromancer to summon Undead Servants for you. They are healed the same way as regular Drowned Servants.

Should a Drowned Necromancer fall, having an $(l:crafts/empty_soul_jar)Empty Soul Jar$() will cause their soul to fill it, which, when right-clicked on a Drowned, will revive them using said Drowned as their new body.

Guardians are strange creatures that may or may not be some sort of flesh-golem creature, similar to Creepers and Shulkers. Unlike those two, probably, these creatures can age and become a stronger specimen at a very old age.

With the mystical Aging Cream, you're able age up a Guardian into an Elder Guardian, making it not only bigger and stronger, but also gives it the knowledge to magically give Mining Fatigue III to nearby non-allied entities similar to yourself.

Usually when a Villager sleeps next to a Nether Portal, they have a chance of turning into a Heretic. When wearing an Unholy Hat and Robe while being near them however, will cause them to not only turn to heresy, but also serve you as loyal acolytes.

You're also able to trade with your Heretic Servant by giving them an Emerald, without needing to wear appropriate attire to do so. You can also trade with other Heretic Servants, provided you're allied to their master, if they have one, and wearing the appropriate attire.
While turning a Pig into a Piglin remains a mystery, turning one into a Hoglin just requires a bunch of Nether Warts and some savagery.

After learning more on the Illagers, how they came about from an ancient struggle where their Villager ancestors took up arms to defend themselves, you've conceived and found a way to introduce violence within the hearts of the Villagers... along with servitude.

While you've managed to turn the pacifistic Villager towards violence, such hatred must be learned. The Illagers don't instantly know how to shoot their crossbows and chop with axes from the get go. To make a proper Illager, one must set up a $(l:goety:crafts/artifice/ominous_pyre)proper training ground$() for them to grow. If one has a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants#banner)registered banner$(), giving a Neollager any banner that's not already a replica and having a Loom near them will have them work to make a replicated banner. Baby Neollagers are quicker to train.
That being said, not all Illagers are made equal. Only those born with the talent for magic can hope to become a spellcaster, whom are conveniently marked by their purple robes.

While armed with the sophisticated crossbow, these Illagers are quite simple in their approach to combat. Fortunately your servants knows how to back off when their target goes near them. They can accept custom arrows by right-clicking on them with up a stack of them, which they will use up when shooting.

Highly trained Pillagers trained to protect their superiors by pelting foes with powerful arrows from behind their shields. You've made this role through creative thinking while researching on desert scrolls.
These highly trained and disciplined Illagers are capable of stabbing targets further from their position.

Though shunned by others for their lack of magic or martial skills, these Illagers are highly useful for spotting incoming threats from afar, especially when perched high up, and sounding a horn that causes Guarding servants in a large radius around themselves, to attack it. These threats are either a hostile Player, a hostile mob with twice the amount of max health as the Signaler or a horde of enemies, the size of which depending on what comprises them and whether they have a higher max health than the Signaler.

One of the most deadliest Illagers now under your command, these brutes can disable shields with their axes and deal a ton of damage as well. You probably shouldn't name them 'Johnny' if you wish to keep them obedient.

A specialized Vindicator that can collect ingredients, like uncooked meat, and will either cook them at a nearby Smoker or Furnace, or assemble them at a nearby Crafting Table into an actual meal. Shift-right click with an empty hand on them will give you their first food in their inventory.
These mountain climbers are a bit more sturdier than their vindictive cousins, both in health and their resistance on being blown away by wind.

These Illagers are usually the ones that forge weapons for other Illagers, but they can also smash apart their foes with their mighty hammer. They can also take ore from a chest they're bound to and smelt them at a nearby Furnace or Blast Furnace, and will also craft weapons to other Illagers if they're somehow deprived of them, or make a better version if they have the resources and the Illager in question doesn't have an enchanted weapon. They're also capable of creating Repair Putties, which they will use to repair nearby damaged golems.

High-ranking Illagers charged with guarding their superiors through intimidation and powerful blows from their maces. If they're shield-less, right click on them with an Iron Ingot to give them their shield back when they're not attacking.

A practitioner of the dark arts, though one that's limited to only two spells, spells they perform quite well though. Combat-wise they love to run around in order to avoid getting stabbed. If their master learned $(l:rumors/ravaging)the ways of ravaging$(), they are able to transform a Villager into a Ravaged, or a Pillager into a Trampler, which requires $(l:goety:focuses/command_focus)commanding$() a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants#banner)leading$() Evoker to one, or a Villager nearby if Villagers as a whole are $(l:goety:crafts/grimoire_of_grudges)grudged against$(), while also having two Evokers nearby.

These scholars have the ability to enchant nearby allies, when confronted with an enemy, increasing their stats and resistance to damage. They can only maintain their links for a time, and it will break if the enchanted moves too far from the Enchanter.
With the ability to manipulate the very ground, these ragged spellcasters can raise stone pillars out of the ground to either hinder their enemy's path or to blow them up.
These chilling conjurers of ice will smash their foes' head with their Ice Chunks.
Ever-crying, these priests of the cold can breath out frost, summon frozen walls to hinder their foes and summon clouds of hail above them.
Masters of the skies, these big haired shamans can fling their foes to the sky or blast them away with the wind.
Whether they're hunting treasures or keeping them safe, these illagers will mercilessly electrocute their enemies to cinders.

The Illagers can be given certain types of food directly or throwing it at them, which they would eat to regenerate health when hurt or to breed. If fully healed, not in combat, not in following mode and with a reachable bed nearby, the food can be used to help them breed with one another, much like Villagers, which would result in a baby Neollager.
pages.title: Food, Breed & Heal

pages.text: Having an excess amount of food in their inventory will cause them to share some food other Illagers with less food. The food they can take are either cooked meat, vegetables, fruits and Rotten Flesh, though they don't eat the latter, but use it to feed $(l:goety:mutations/ravaged)Ravaged or injured Ravagers$(). They can also be given armor to wear and associated weapons to equip.

While the Illagers have their own ominous banner, it would be both fun and useful to have your own banner that signifies your rule. To register your own personal banner, simply place down a banner and right click it with a Wand or Staff that doesn't have a Block based spell (ie, $(l:goety:focuses/geomancy/pulverize_focus)Pulverize$()).
pages.title: Personal Banner

pages.text: Illagers like Pillager Servants can be made a captain.
pages.name: Illager Captain

pages.text: If an Illager were given your $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants#banner)personal banner$(), they will become a captain. Using a $(l:goety:focuses/command_focus)Command$() / $(l:goety:focuses/order_focus)Order$() Focus and commanding Illagers and certain other raiding servants, like tamed Ravagers, onto a leading Illager will cause them to follow them instead of you. Updating their movement stance will stop them from following the leading Illager. Right-clicking on the captain with an empty hand will cause them to drop their banner.

Right-clicking on a captain with a Taglock Kit, that has a Tagged creature on it, will cause them, and nearby raiding servants that are following the Illager, or not have a captain, to hunt said creature down before returning to their master once they slay their query. If the hunting party contains raiders that weren't following any Illager, they will start to follow the captain they came with.

Right-clicking on an Illager captain with a Waystone, that stored a position located in a chunk-loaded Village, with a Goat, or Raiding, Horn offhand, will cause them to perform a raid on the Village, attacking all non-baby Villagers. Much like with the taglock, the captain will cause nearby leaderless raiders to join them.
pages.title: Raiding

pages.text: If their raid is successful, they will return to their master and will drop off loot, as Illagers gain Emeralds and other loot when killing Villagers. They will not perform a raid if their master has stored Villagers as a whole as $(l:goety:crafts/grimoire_of_goodwill)allies$(). To stop your raid, either register Villagers as your $(l:goety:crafts/grimoire_of_goodwill)allies$() or press Ceasefire key $(l)while holding a banner on main or offhand$().
All Illagers will collect any loot from their kills and will throw them at their master when they're near them and away from combat, unless the loot is a valid food for them to eat.

Right-clicking on a Raider with an Ominous Shackles will cause them to enter Capturing Mode where, rather than killing Villagers, they will turn them into $(l:goety:mutations/prisoners)Prisoners$() that will follow their captor and can be commanded by you. Right-clicking on the Capturing raider with Shears will stop them from being in Capturing Mode.
pages.title: Capturing

pages.text: Much like everything else, all raiders will enter Capturing Mode if their captain is in that mode. In Raids, if all surviving Villagers are Prisoners, the raid is considered a success. The Prisoner can be chained to you if you right-click on them, and can be chained to a captain by right-clicking on them with an empty hand. There's a chance that certain Villagers don't end up being captured and can potentially die like usual.

Right clicking on an Illager with a Waystone that leads to an unlocked Chest will cause them to register the chest as a valid container to take food from it, or store excess food and loot, when they are nearby. If the Illager is a leader, their followers will register the same chest as well.
pages.title: Chest Interaction

pages.text: An Illager can also register another chest aside from regular ones. When registered to this, Illagers will try to deposit any loot they have in this above their other chest and will not take items from it.

Illagers can be given armor (if config is set to true) and can be given a Totem of Undying so long as their offhand is empty. Right-clicking on them with a Stick will cause them to drop their Totem from their Offhand.

Some items can be given to an Illager that gives them additional abilities. Simply right-click on an Illager to equip them a charm, right-click on them with a Stick to remove any charms they're equipped with (if they're no longer/not holding a Totem offhand).
pages.title: Charms

pages.text: Mavericks appear to be highly devoted to the Nether that they only obey those that are highly devoted to it. However, wearing the Unholy set near a trader that's underneath a block of Crying Obsidian will cause the newly convert to see you as a master of the Nether and obey your commands.

You're also able to trade with your Maverick Servant by giving them an Emerald, without needing to wear appropriate attire to do so. You can also trade with other Maverick Servants, provided you're allied to their master, if they have one, and wearing the appropriate attire.
With some red mushrooms and a cow, you're able to turn said cow into a red Mooshroom.
The scroll contains some instruction on granting, or calling forth, intelligence to the long diseased, allowing you to create and command undead Necromancers from Skeletons.
The Necromancers can be taught to summon more than just Zombies. Right-clicking with certain Necromancy Focuses allows them to summon more types of servants.

They will only accept focuses that summons an undead creature they can't already summon themselves. They can accept Rotting Focus, Osseous Focus, Spooky Focus, Reaping Focus, Vanguard Focus and Blackguard Focus.
Right-clicking on them with an empty hand will cause the Necromancer to summon Undead Servants for you. They are healed the same way as regular Skeleton Servants.

Should a Necromancer fall, having an $(l:crafts/empty_soul_jar)Empty Soul Jar$() will cause their soul to fill it, which, when right-clicked on a Skeleton, will revive them using said Skeleton as their new body. It's also rumored that feeding them with a jar of another necromancer will increase their power...
Not really a mutation unless one considers being chained and captured to fall under the concept.

Prisoners that follow mobs will follow them like any other servants, but when directly following you, as seen by them being chained to you, they will follow much like they're tied by a lead. Prisoners, when on 'Guarding' mode, will not wander around the area like other servants, but will stay put but are still able to move to interact with certain objects.
To free a Prisoner, right-click on them while crouching. Prisoners can also be freed if they have taken enough damage while away from their captor or owner.
Right-clicking on a Prisoner with a Pickaxe of any kind allows them to enter Mining Mode. First, they must be near ores, then they must not be in Following mode in order for them to start mining.
pages.title: Prisoner Mines

pages.text: Prisoners will collect ore drops once in a while, but will stop mining once either their pickaxe wore out, if they become hungry, or their inventory is full. They will either give their mined goods to an Illager or, if bounded to a chest, place them in it. Right-clicking on them with an empty hand while they're mining will cause them to face towards you, and angle they will face when they start to mine again if they stopped before. Right-click on them with a Stick to make them drop their pickaxe.
When mining, Prisoners will get hungry, and will stop mining once they begin to starve.
pages.title: Hunger

pages.text: To feed them, either directly give them food or put them into a chest they're bound to. Your Illager servants will also feed the prisoners if they have excess amount of food, funnily enough.

Right clicking on a Prisoner with a Waystone that leads to an unlocked Chest will cause them to register the chest as a valid container to store their drops. If the chest, they're bounded to, have pickaxes, and a Servant or their Master is nearby, they will take it if they're not holding anything.
pages.title: Chest Interaction

pages.text: A Prisoner can also register another chest aside from regular ones. When registered to this, Prisoners will try to deposit any loot they have in this above their other chest and will not take items from it.

The secrets of creating Ravagers have been revealed to you. As you have long suspected, Ravagers are made from average Villagers through magical means. The conversion, however, is not instantaneous. The Villager is turned into, what it's called, Ravaged, and will need to consume large amount of flesh before it can transition into a full Ravager.

The Ravaged can be fed by throwing Rotten Flesh at it, or siccing them onto any Villager, or Illager surprisingly, and have them kill the latter. Unsurprisingly, Villagers provide the most amount of flesh than any other. Once the Ravaged has transformed, it would need a specialized saddle that will make it not only rideable, but also stronger.
Fully grown Ravagers can be part of a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)raiding party$(), though they cannot be leaders.

Lately, Wandering Traders seems to transform when shot with Lightning, you began pondering if you can make a servant out of Reprobates much like you did with Witches. After a while, you discovered that some Soul Energy, a Magic Emerald and a Mystic Core can turn a bumbling trader into a loyal Reprobate.

You're also able to trade with your Reprobate Servant by giving them an Emerald, without needing to wear appropriate attire to do so. You can also trade with other Reprobate Servants, provided you're allied to their master, if they have one, and wearing the appropriate attire.
You've learned how to fast track the Illager's domestication wolves into Rippers, using dark magic.
Rippers are healed and bred with meat, the same way as regular wolves. They also grow up faster than regular wolves.
Rippers can be part of a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)raiding party$(), though they cannot be leaders.
Despite its boniness, the steed can not only withstand being ridden without breaking under weight, but can also ride underwater.
It appears you've found a way to create a violent horse-like steed made from Illagers instead of Villagers.
Much like camels, pressing jump will charge up their dash, allowing you to manually charge at your foes.
Tramplers can be part of a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)raiding party$(), though they cannot be leaders.
Having an oath breaker as a servant might raise some eyebrows, but nonetheless you've discovered how to do so. With the infernal air of the Nether, you can turn a Villager into a loyal Warlock.

You're also able to trade with your Warlock Servant by giving them an Emerald, without needing to wear appropriate attire to do so. You can also trade with other Warlock Servants, provided you're allied to their master, if they have one, and wearing the appropriate attire.
With some testing and studying, you've managed to recreate one of the Nephilim's greatest folly, though without the whole betrayal thing of course.

The master of blazes can be healed by right-clicking it with Blaze Powders or Rods, and can passively heal if their owner dons a Nether Robe, much like their lesser brethren. So intune to fire, they regenerate when standing on one and heal when struck by fiery attacks (with some... exceptions).
When extinguished, these fiery overlords will drop their helms which can elevate a Blaze to their level.

While turning Villagers into Witches is a well known science, you wondered how to make Witch that serves you. Fortunately some Soul Energy, and a lot of Emeralds and a Mystic Core, allows one to make a loyal Witch.

You're also able to trade with your Witch Servant by giving them an Emerald, without needing to wear appropriate attire to do so. You can also trade with other Witch Servants, provided you're allied to their master, if they have one, and wearing the appropriate attire.

You've discovered a more powerful variant of regular Necromancers, one that burns with the fires of the Nether, shooting jets of flames from the ground and withers their foes. Rather than regular Skeletons, the ritual is performed on a Wither Skeleton instead.

Much like regular Necromancers, they can be taught to summon more than just Wither Skeletons. Right-clicking with certain Necromancy Focuses allows them to summon more types of servants. Right-clicking on them with an empty hand will cause the Necromancer to summon Undead Servants for you. They are healed the same way as regular Wither Skeleton Servants.

Should a Wither Necromancer fall, having an $(l:crafts/empty_soul_jar)Empty Soul Jar$() will cause their soul to fill it, which, when right-clicked on a Wither Skeleton, will revive them using said Wither Skeleton as their new body.
A rotten steed for a rotten wizard, these undead horses are much more docile and quicker than any Zombies you know.

You know what's better than a regular Ravager? An Undead one! Well, kinda. Much like most Undead, the Zombie Ravager would burn in sunlight, and can't swim in water. The Zombie Ravager is also slower than its living counter part, but has a tiny boost in Armor points. Overall, a perfect mount for a Necromancer or for someone who hates sunlight and love rotting corpses.
Fighting a foe with their own Arca can be a real struggle, for finding it can take a lot of time and guesswork. Fortunately, you've devised a way to locate your foe's Arca with a specialized compass.

Killing your foe while holding the compass on either hands will cause it to bind towards the player. If the player moves, places down or bind with an Arca, the compass will automatically point to its location.
You've heard rumors of powerful magicians that once roam the Nether Fortresses. It is said that a specific incantation could summon one forth when cast within said fortress.
With a Goat's horn and the power of the Nether, you can replicate the incantation to summon forth one of these beings.

Just because you're a dark wizard doesn't mean you can't be decorative. These braziers are a fancy way of providing light and burn any fool that stand on them when lit. The braziers can also be unlit by right-clicking on them, and relit the same way.
Like torches and campfires, these braziers can also burn with soul fire.

You've managed to obtain a manuscript that details on the fortress dwellers workings and magic. Unfortunately, the manuscript is nigh-unreadable but you've managed to find a way to call upon the dead to fill in the blanks.

The Commanding Horn allows you to change movement stances of your servants, that are within 4 blocks from you, and comes with multiple modes that can be changed by shift-right clicking while holding it.
On None mode, the horn makes the servants go between Standing By and Following. On others it will cause all servant nearby to enter the mode the horn is set to.

You can also right click on a block to have them move towards it, unless the servants are guarding and the horn is not in Guard mode. However, servants that are already commanded or part of a $(l:crafts/grimoire_of_grounding)Grimoire of Grounding$() are unaffected by the horn.

Using a Command Horn on None mode while having a filled $(l:crafts/patrol_plan)Patrol Plan$() offhand will cause all selected servants to patrol at the positions. Blowing it while shift right-clicking will stop selected servants from patrolling.
Magical cores are used to create all kinds of spells and equipments and can be crafted through all kinds of rituals.
The $(l:intro/magical_components)Empty Focus$() is the core for all magical Focuses.
pages.title: Empty Focus

pages.text: A decorative block that changes textures when placed on one another.

These essences dropped by that $(l:world/bestiary/wight)horrific creature$() appears to be resonating towards something. By combining it with an Eye of Ender, you've discovered that instead of leading to the nearest Stronghold, it leads to $(l:world/crypts)someplace else$().
It appears that using it will throw a copy of the eye instead of using it fully. However, it takes up durability when doing so.

You've done it, you've managed to channel the energies of the Deep Dark into a metal that repairs itself using Soul Energy. The amount of Soul Energy needed to craft one ingot is very substantial, but you've managed regardless. The metal appears to be highly malleable and practical and almost as enchantable as Gold. It also appears to slow down and weaken any creature it was struck at.

You've heard whispers of a High Ranking Illager, and how they occasionally call upon or answer the calls of other Illagers to give out commands and advice. You believe they hold something very powerful that can increase your magical powers.
With the Evoker's Totem, you can trick one of these Illagers to answer your call.
(Recommended Equipment: Enchanted Armor)
With some Shade Stone, you're able to create a jar that can hold a soul of a certain Servants that, when used on certain entities, revives them.
Apparently delving into the dark arts gives you knowledge of making new block variants for End Stone and Purpur Blocks.

Growing tired of Servants losing their way to you, and/or using Call and Troop Focuses from afar, you've desperately wished you could just put your servants into your pocket so that you can unleash them wherever you wish.

After countless days of research and experimentation, you've created an odd box that fulfills your desire. By left-clicking one of your servants with it, it will instantly contain them. Holding down right-click will slowly pull out your servants from it, but will use up durability that will render it unusable until repaired, which can be done on an Anvil with Ender Pearls. It can hold multiple servants, and is immune to being burned in fire and lava. If destroyed while in thrown form, it will release every servant within itself.

There are some conditions when it comes to storing certain types of servants. Some servants take up more than one space within the tesseract, depending on their size, (and whether they're tagged properly). Limited life servants will have their lifespan paused when stored within the tesseract.

Unless one builds a base around a Monster Spawner, it can be quite tedious going back and forth from the block. It's unfortunate one cannot simply pick a up the arcane device and bring it where ever one goes. Unless...
The cage can capture the flaming core of the Spawner, breaking the block in the process.

Once the cage captures the Spawner's core, it can be right-clicked onto an empty $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$() where it will convert it into a copy of the original Spawner, making the Cursed Infusion process and Mob Farming more convenient! Although doing this so will destroy the item in the process.

The Forbidden Grass Block calls upon the creatures of the night that roam within the biome the block is placed in. Mobs will spawn more quickly on the block but generally follows the rules of how they spawn, ex. Light Level. The Block will burn in sunlight and will catch fire from adjacent blocks which will revert it to Dirt.
The Block will drop as Dirt if not collected with Silk Touch.

When the dead are buried, the soil can become infused with necrotic energies, giving it a chance of reanimating the corpse and turning back into dark dirt once more, if there's no blocks placed atop of it.

An upgraded version of the humble $(l:intro/cursed_infuser)Cursed Infuser$(), where not only can it transform Obsidian to Crypt Stone, but also accept and infuse more than one item. Works the same way as its previous counterpart.
Sometimes, your servants can be detrimental to your plans, attacking creatures it wasn't supposed to, causing you to shout at them to stop attacking for example.

The grimoire can record multiple beings, from Pillagers to even beings like you! You can also prevent servants from attacking an entire species, as hitting a being while crouching will record the being's species. For example, crouching and hitting a Pillager with the grimoire will cause your servants to no longer attack all Pillagers, even if they're pelting you with arrows.
Right clicking in the air shows who you have goodwill with. Shift right click to see the species.

However, if you're in a vengeful mood and want to erase the goodwill, you can simply right click on the being you have goodwill with, or shift right click if you have a goodwill with the entire species, the goodwill will be erased from the grimoire. Until you left-click on them again.
Adding goodwill to a being or species that's recorded on the Grimoire of Grudges will erase the grudge.

Sometimes, you want some of your servants, or their subspecies so to speak, to stay where they are when mass teleporting them through crouch casting their associated summoning spell or through other spells.

When mentioning recording their subspecies, what it means is that if you were to add Jungle Zombie Servants to it, crouch casting Rotting Spell will summon all variants of Zombie Servants except for Jungle.
Right clicking in the air shows who you have grounded. Shift right click to see the species.

Call Spell still works even if stored summon is recorded in the grimoire. For Troop Spell, only individuals recorded on the grimoire aren't teleported. The grimoire adds and erases servants the same way other grimoires do for creatures.
The grimoire also prevents temporary servants recorded in it to be dismissed via the 'Dismiss Temporary Servants' key.

Sometimes, you feel like you have an intense grudge against a certain being, yet your servants won't attack them unprovoked! Fortunately, you've devised a terrible book, one that when hitting that being with it causes it to record them.

Any being recorded in this grimoire will cause all your servants to be automatically hostile towards said being. The grimoire can record multiple beings, ranging from Villagers to even beings like you! That's not all, if your grudge extends towards species, hitting the being while crouching will cause the being's species be recorded! For example, crouching and hitting a Villager with the grimoire will make all your servants hostile towards ALL Villagers.
Right clicking in the air shows who you're grudging against. Shift right click to see the species.

However, if you're in a forgiving mood and want to erase the grudge, you can simply right click on the being you have a grudge with, or shift right click if you have a grudge against the entire species, the grudge will be erased from the grimoire. Until you hit them again.
Adding grudge to a being or species that's recorded on the Grimoire of Goodwill will erase the goodwill.

Haunted Armor Stands are somewhat different than regular Armor Stands as unlike the latter, the stand comes with arms to put weapons or items for it to hold. Due to being made of Haunted Planks, the stand is immune to fire.
What truly makes the stand special, is that if the stand is fully clad in armor, right-clicking an Animation Core on it will transform the stand into a loyal Haunted Armor.
pages.title: Haunted Armor

pages.text: Haunted Armors can be healed by right-clicking on them with Ectoplasm.
Combining a regular painting with a Haunted Plank allows the creation of Haunted Paintings. Despite the name, they appear to be a new set of paintings and nothing more.
You have successfully recreated the scroll and finally unravelled its secret. The ultimate art of Necroturgy, to cast away mortality and walk as the king of the dead.

To become a Lich, you must brew a special Necroturgic Potion, The Potion of Transformation. With the use of the Apostle's blood, several other ingredients and a sacrifice of a Villager, you will be able to cast a Necroturgic Ritual to brew such a foul potion. The Ritual requires a large amount of Soul Energy, far larger than what a Totem of Souls can usually carry.

However, one should not immediately drink the brew once crafted! The brew must be drunk on a Full Moon. You must also have an $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$() ready to bind your soul to it. Once drunk, you will die, but will rise as an Undead creature if all goes to plan. (If on Hardcore, make sure your Totem is full, or hold a Totem of Undying offhand!)

Marble is a fancy looking block found on the highest peaks of the world. Unfortunately, such peaks are far beyond your reach, but with Soul Energy, Cursed Infusion and Calcite, you can get these wondrous blocks for yourself.
Indented Gold blocks, while less shiny than a full Block of Gold, are still capable of being symbols of pure opulence and wealth. An odd building block for what you've heard as an ancient sanctum.

Highrock blocks are said to be the rocks that make up the tallest peaks of the world. From what you've heard, they seemed to be a variant of Andesite and its polished version is used on the highest forges.
Cragrocks are also said to make up the peaks of the world, being used to make walls for the villages up there and pavement.
Siltstones are strange blocks that have the most variable looks from other blocks. They can be messy and combine with marble and jade, but also be used to make several decorative blocks.

The dark arts is a pathway to many abilities some consider to be... pretty? Your journey through the dark arts has lead you to discover several decorations that lets you feel more like a true dark wizard.
Ironically, one of the things you've found are better ways to light up your lair.

Normal carpets don't cut out for you. The floors of your lair needs to be more opulent for your feet to walk on. Unfortunately, your carpets need to be put into pieces for you to combine into a proper carpet way.

What good is a lair without a throne to sit on? You can even have a Servant sit on one, by either commanding them to it, or have them guard, through waystone or command, on the position of the throne. To get them off, you can command them off, set them to guard another position, or simply dismiss them.

Thrones of all types can be enchanted with Royalty through a Ritual. Not only will no one but you or your allies can sit on the throne, but sitting on it will cause up to 4 nearby allies to take up incoming damage towards you. If someone else breaks the throne, it will lose its enchantment.
pages.title: Royalty

pages.text: You've infused a candlestick with large amounts of necrotic energies, causing it to burn baleful green flames once lit. The flames appear shield the undead, or beings like you for some reason, within 8 blocks from it, from the sun, though not fire, allowing them to move in daylight without burning.

If both candlestick and undead beings, within 8 blocks of it, are not exposed to the sun, whether they be beneath a ceiling or it's night time, they will slowly heal themselves, so long as it remains lit.
Based on @kiko5836's suggestion

The $(l:mutations/ravaged)Ravager$() is a powerful beast, yet the one you have lacks its silver armor and saddle. With some $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal$(), you are able to recreate the armored saddle. Right-clicking on the poor naked $(l:mutations/ravaged)Ravager$() will cause it to equip it, making it rideable and stronger.
Villagers can hard to wrangle, with the common technique of putting them in a boat makes one look silly when riding on land. With these shackles, you won't be having trouble moving them that much.
Using these on Villagers or Wandering Traders will turn them into $(l:mutations/prisoners)Prisoners$().
These blocks seems to resonate well with the Illagers. Perhaps they can be seen as the stone to their beloved Dark Oak.
By breaking Ominous Stone, you can obtain its cobbled counterpart. Much like regular cobblestone, you can smelt it to obtain Ominous Stone.
pages.title: Cobbled Ominous Stone

pages.text: Using a Pickaxe on a Cobbled Ominous Stone will turn it into a path the same way dirt paths are made with shovels.
pages.title: Cobbled Ominous Stone Path

pages.text: Wall Shrines can be attached to sides of a block and functions as decoration.
These statues are made in the likeness of an ancient illager warrior. Their brazier counterparts can have their fire put out or ignited by right-clicking on them.
pages.title: Ominous Statues

pages.text: Most roots and flora out in nature are too weak and feeble for certain parts of wild magic. Fortunately, you've managed to devise some strong roots that can handle such magical powers.

You've been confused over the metal found on the shoulderpads and belt of Pillagers and the armor of Ravagers. Are they Silver? Platinum? Odd colored Iron? Desaturated Diamond? After some testing and 'negotiating' you've discovered that it's, in a way, all of them.

Some are silver, some are platinum, some are just colored iron and so on. They just look and, in some cases, act the same to you. You've decided to recreate the most common type of the illager metal as silver and platinum might not be available, or probably too valuable, to use for dark purposes.

This parchment can hold multiple positions for your servants to patrol around. Simply record your positions and right-click the parchment on your servant for them to start patrolling. To stop your servants from patrolling, simply change their movement mode or shift right-clicking on them with the plan.

Using a $(l:crafts/command_horn)Command Horn$() on None mode while having a filled Patrol Plan offhand will cause all selected servants to patrol at the positions. Blowing it while shift right-clicking will stop selected servants from patrolling.

The Blood of an Apostle allows one to craft the mythical Philosopher's Stone. With this, one can duplicate gold by putting this stone with raw gold. Doing this will cause the stone to take durability, but it can repair itself using Soul Energy.

With bamboos to make the vines and kelp sturdier, and some bone meals, you've made seeds that will quickly grow into a $(l:summons/quick_growing_vines)strong sentient vine$(), or kelp when placed underwater, that can block a creature's way.
Crouching while placing one down will cause the vine to be inert, only growing once a valid enemy or target comes near it.

Mixing the seed with a cave spider's toxins and corpse blossoms will sprout poison quill vines, that will shoot poisonous quills at your foes. Much like the Quick Growing Seeds, crouching will cause it to be inert and will grow once an enemy is near.
The horn allows you to cause your $(l:mutations/illager_servants#raid)Raiders$() to start raiding the village you're in when used.

While reading the scroll on the secrets of $(l:mutations/ravaged)Ravagers$(), you've came up with an idea of creating specialize armor that augments their already $(l:crafts/ominous_saddle)armored saddles$().

Creating armor for the massive beast requires a lot of Iron and metal but it will provide a large amount of protection for the newly transformed $(l:mutations/ravaged)Ravager$(). However, the $(l:mutations/ravaged)Ravager$() must be $(l:crafts/ominous_saddle)Saddled$() before applying the armor. You've heard rumors that you're not the first to think of armoring up Ravagers...
A miraculous substance that can be applied onto a living construct or golem of any material and repair them, so long as the user holds a hammer offhand.
Sarcophagi functions the same as beds, but instead of sleeping through the night, you sleep through the day instead.

You can also cushion your sarcophagus by right-clicking on it with wool, making it more comfortable to lay in. You can also change the color of the cushions by right-clicking the sarcophagus with dye, or remove the cushions by using Shears.
pages.title: Cushioning

pages.text: You've discovered a new type of fungus that can only grow on Crimson or Warped Stems/Hyphae called Snap Fungus. The Fungus is a ball full of toxins that one can't help but throw upwards in the air. When hitting something, they will explode, with a chance of leaving behind a small cloud of poison. Curiously, the explosion does not effect the thrower nor their servants.
It appears that you can only throw a large amount of them at a time. On one hand, you get to throw multiple at once, on the other, you can't throw any more for a couple of seconds.
You've also discovered a way to increase the potency of the fungi by combining 4 of them with a Ghast Tear. These fungi's explosions have larger radius but no longer leave any poison clouds.

By putting Snap Fungi with a Lily of the Valley in a Brewing Stand, you've managed to create the Berserk Fungus. Unlike the other two fungi, the fungus throws much like Snowballs and Eggs, and grants whoever gets hit with Strength, Speed and, unfortunately for beings like you, Nausea.
$(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cages$() are fine and dandy, but you're starting to get sick of constantly putting and removing your precious totem from them.
Fortunately, with power of Activated Emeralds, you have found a way to transfer Soul Energies from an $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$() to a $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$().

Simply right-click the Transfer Gem on the $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$() and it will bound to it and it's owner. Then, put the Transfer Gem within the $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$() and it will siphon Soul Energy from the $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$() when it's being used.
A simple urn that holds emeralds within itself, that can even break apart and reveal its content when shot with a projectile.
A taglock kit is used to collect taglocks from creatures or rivals. Taglocks are used to create a link between target and witchcraft.

To collect taglocks, simply left click the kit on a being. One can also obtain a taglock by right-clicking it on a bed that's been used by a beings like yourself. For some reason, you can't obtain Villager taglocks this way.
Be warn! While tagging a creature is a simple matter, tagging a fellow being like yourself requires a more sneaky approach, as they can notice your failed attempt!
The blueprint shares some similarities with the Warred Scroll, making you think that transcribing it into a readable schematic requires something that's from a similar creation.
While $(l:crafts/ravager_armor)armoring$() $(l:mutations/ravaged)Ravagers$() is good step, you've realized that their lanky counterparts would also benefit from being armored as well.

Creating armor for these beasts are cheaper than making Ravager armor, their shape and method of transportation requires the use of horse armor to make their own version. You've heard that much like Ravagers, you're not the first to think of this idea...
Whether through trade or a way to aid your allies, you have devise a scroll that will transfer ownership of one of your Servants to the recipient.

To start, one must left-click the scroll onto their servant to sign it. Once signed, any beings like yourself can use the scroll and have the servant signed on it serve them instead, so be mindful on using and storing these signed parchments.

The echoes of the dead and the remnant thoughts within the Nether could hold some secrets towards a dark power. With the power of echo shards and some necroturgy, you are able to create a piece of a dark, and sinister power.
You've heard of interesting blocks and liquids found in the End that are harmful to those that thread upon them, unless they are spawns of the End themselves...

To obtain a Bottle of Void, you must use an empty Glass Bottle below the dimension's minimum build height, -64 Y for the Overworld, 0 for both the Nether and the End, though one can say it's easier to obtain in the End as it has no Bedrock blocking the Void.
To obtain a Bucket of Liquid Void, fill a Cauldron with Bottles of Void and use a Bucket on it.

Both Void Blocks and Liquid will inflict damage that's equal to 5%% of max health per second, while also giving and amplifying Void Touched effect to creatures that move through them. Enderman, Endermites and Enderlings are immune to the effects, but not Shulkers strangely enough.

A Void Barrel is a volatile block that will unleash an explosion of void when set off, breaking itself in the process. To set the barrel off, either right-click on it, activate it with redstone or shoot a projectile at it.
Liquid Void can also create decorative blocks when interacted with either Water or Lava. Pouring Water on source Liquid Void will turn it into Void Block.

When a flowing water meets flowing void, it creates End Soil. Not only can Chorus Flowers grow on them, but having lava flow onto it with Blue Ice adjacent will create renewable Obsidian. Bone mealing on it will create some plants that seems to be related to Chorus Plants.
One can also create a sapling from the void, which provides a new set of wood-like blocks that are not burnable. They can only be planted on End Soil.
Growing 4 Chorus Saplings in a 2x2 area will create a gigantic Chorus Tree that has Corrupted Chorus Logs, which also provide another set of wood-like blocks, or Liquid Void within itself.
You've discovered a way to make an ecosystem using this growth. It can be used to create, or right-clicked on certain end-related blocks, to create foliage.
Bone mealing these blocks will grow Chorus Ferns and Chorus Tall Grass on top of them. Chorus Grass Blocks can spread to adjacent Smooth End Stones.

You've also discovered another type of foliage that can be introduced in the End, one that looks fleshy and seems to grow vines, when applied bone meal, similar to Twisting Vines of the Nether. End Growth Blocks can spread to adjacent End Rocks.
Applying Void directly to dirt seems to make it purple and untillable by hoe, but it can grow some Chorus Stalks when bone mealed and be used as terrain decoration. It can spread to other dirt.
Chorus Saplings can be planted on both End Growth Blocks and End Dirt but, when fully grown, instead of having yellow leaves, they grow leaves that look more like Chorus Flowers.

Applying a Water Bottle on an End Soil will turn it into End Mud. Using a Glass Bottle on it will turn it back to End Soil, but will give you End Mud Bottle, which can filled into a Cauldron to make a Cauldron of End Mud.
Filling a Bucket with the content of a full cauldron will give a Bucket of Liquid End Mud, which functions similar to Water, except it does not damage beings of The End and spreads a bit slowly.

You don't know what compels you, but you've decided to cover an Eye of Ender with the essence of the Void, which ends up making a special eye that leads to $(l:world/final_terminal)a place of power$().
It appears that using it will throw a copy of the eye instead of using it fully. However, it takes up durability when doing so.
Surrounding a Spider Egg with Nether Warts seems to create a fertilized egg that spawns a Wartling. Spawning a Wartling would hurt the user a bit as it takes a bit of life force from them.

Waystones allows you to bound it to a specific location by simply right-clicking a block with it, which can be used to perform all kinds of dark magic upon it, assuming that said location is in the same dimension.
The stone also marks the holder as its owner when used.

Right-clicking a bound waystone on certain servants will cause them to start guarding around that location, putting them into Guarding mode, so long as the location is in the same dimension. Shift-right clicking a bound waystone will erase the information it has stored within itself.

The Abyss Robes allows you to harness the power of the oceans far more efficiently and effectively. The Robes makes the wearer swim faster, and reduces the damage from drowning, even providing a small amount of air after taking damage.
Loyal water creatures will slowly heal themselves using their summoner's soul energy, should the summoner don this robe.
The Abyss Crown reduce the amount of time to cast Abyss spells by half and keeps your water servants from dying off like Vexes.

When hunting you down, the Illagers tend to signal their approach by having rows of fangs below you, or a Tormentor charging at you. With how sneaky they are, you've managed to devise a charm that would signal their arrival towards you.

Evokers wear such snazzy robes, that you wonder if they're just for show or there's something special about them. By utilizing Dark and Magic Fabrics, you've managed to not only replicate their Robes, but also make some new additions, and discover they hold some special properties.
The Robes worn by Evokers help channel their magic more efficiently, utilizing 15%% of the Soul Cost needed to cast the spell.
The Dark Hat helps you focus on your spells, reducing the time needed to cast them.
The Dark Crown also reduces the time needed to cast spells. A headwear more fitting for soon-to-be royalty.
The amulet contains the essence of a feline creature on it, making it seemed like the wearer has one on them the whole time, warding off Creepers and Phantoms away.

You find yourself having trouble carrying multiple $(l:focuses)focuses$() on your person. Fortunately, you've managed to devise a leather bag to hold multiple focuses that you can easily access, by either pressing the Focus Bag key (Default: C) or holding a wand and pressing Focus Circle key (Default: X) and can wear on your waist.
The Focus Bag can hold up to 10 focuses.
The Focus Pack can hold up to 20 focuses.

The Frost Robes imbues the wearer the power of all that's cold. Wearers will never freeze, be resistant to Freezing attacks and can move through Powdered Snow freely. The Robes also makes Frost Spells cheaper.
The Frost Crown reduce the amount of time to cast Frost spells by half and keeps certain frost servants from dying off like Vexes.
With pelts and some magical fabrics, this simple shamanistic robe reduces the soul cost of Geomantic spells by half.
Amethysts are powerful conduits to Geomantic magic. By crafting and wearing this necklace, the casting time of Geomantic spells will be reduced by half.
The Vizier has some snazzy robes themselves, and a good looking turban too. With their Ruby, you can replicate these garments and get some of their special abilities!
You feel like you've might as well! You've already took the Evoker's style, why not move up on the world?

While taking damage while wearing the Turban, you will have a 50%%, or a 100%% if you're at or below half of your maximum health, of spawning a loyal Irk that will defend you. If you use the Vexing Spell while crouching, it will kill of your Irks, healing you a heart per killed.

At first, the Robe seems to be just another recolor of the Dark Robes, but when casting a spell through your wand you've discovered that doing so will give you the Vizier's shield, halving all incoming damage so long as you're spellcasting.

Scythes are fun and all, but they're very slow to wield making it hard for them to be a viable weapon. Using the remnants of the dead and Necroturgy, you've managed to create gloves that allow you to wield the Scythes more efficiently, increasing the attack speed by 50%%.

Using the Occult Fabrics, you are able to create a set of Illusive Robes that will make you immune to Blindness effect and turn invisible when you do, making you highly undetectable to mobs and others of your kind.
The robe also buffs the Mirror Spell by making your Doppelgangers' attack actually hurt their targets, though not by a lot.
After discovering the most hidden of necromantic ways, you've devised a new set of garb to showcase your mastery over the dark arts.
The set functions the same as the old Necro Set with some improvements and does not give the wearer debuffs when under sunlight.

The power of commanding Zombies and Skeletons sounds wonderful, but with the power of the Necro Cape, your Necroturgic abilities enhance even further. Wearing it causes your Skeletons' arrows to pass through allied creatures, and Zombies can turn wild Zombies into more Servants that obeys you.

The Necro Crown keeps your undead horde from decaying like Vexes and will reduce the amount of time to cast Necromancy spells by half. Be warned, wearing a Necro Crown in daylight will cause the wearer to gain Weakness, Hunger when wearing the Cape.

With the growing knowledge of the Nether, you've managed to craft a robe that imbues the wearer with its flames. Wearers will be resistant to fire attacks and extinguish fire from them more quickly. The Robes also makes Nether Spells cheaper and Nether servants regenerate using their summoner's soul energy.
The Nether Crown reduce the amount of time to cast Nether spells by half and keeps your nether-spawned servants from dying off like Vexes.

When killing a Patrol Captain, you'll always get cursed with Bad Omen, which can be useful at times, but annoying and detrimental as well. After some research, you've devise a charm that absorbs the dying curse of the captain, sparing you the effect, even if the charm has reached level 5 its maximum level.

Not only that, if you currently have the Bad Omen on you, right-clicking with the charm, or pressing the Activate Curio key if equipped, will absorb it. Should you wish to be afflicted with Bad Omen within the charm, simply right-click with it, or press the Activate Curio key if equipped, if you don't currently have the effect on.

The Pendant of Hunger absorbs any Rotten Flesh in your inventory, storing them within itself and uses it to automatically feed you once you are feeling a bit peckish. Of course, eating such food leaves you more hungry than before.
The Ring of the Dragon, when worn, causes you to emit an explosion, when you teleport with spells, ender pearls or chorus fruits, upon your previous location before entering a small cooldown.
The ring can be enchanted with Radius to increase the size of the explosion.
The Telekinesis spell is fun and all, but what if you want to damage whoever you're holding without constantly smashing them to the ground?
Casting the spell while wearing this ring will cause the being you're holding to slowly lose breath, chocking until they perish or you lose your grip on them.
When summoning a Zombie or Skeleton Servants, they have a small chance of coming equipped with their own armor. With this ring, the chance will increase to 100%%.
If 'illagerServantTrainArmor' is enabled, wearing this ring will cause newly trained Illagers to gain armor.
