The Eerie Pickaxe might be useful for collecting Experience Orbs, there are times where even that ability is not enough. With this ring, experience is immediately given to the wearer if it's dropped by killing a creature, personally or through a servant.

The Ring of Want allows creatures to drop more loot when slain by your spells or by creatures conjured up by you. For the Ring to work, you must enchant it, where it will accept the Wanting Enchantment which functions similar to Looting.
Wearing the Ring of Want with Wanting III or more will cause your Fangs to have a 25%% chance (100%% if it's a Player) of dropping a creature's head/skull.
While some take joy of taking trophies from slain foes, some don't find having their inventory be filled with damaged armor, tools and weapons and having to rid of them to make space to be fun.

Fortunately, this ring will cause those unstackable items to completely break without ever entering your inventory. However, this does not work on creatures like yourself and any items given to your servants will also not break if you personally dismiss them.

The Sea Amulet provides the effect Conduit Power towards the wearer whenever they're underwater, using up its inner charges. In order to charge the amulet, the wearer must be 8 blocks near an active Conduit underwater. The amulet will only provide its effect if the wearer doesn't have it or when the previous effect is 5 seconds away from expiring.
A common amongst Illagers within Woodland Mansions, these artifacts heals the user the same way casting the $(l:focuses/soul_heal_focus)Soul Heal spell$() does.

You can also give a Soul Healer to an Illager servant, where they will now take and store half of the soul energy per kill into the trinket, and will use it once they have enough and they're below half of their max health, where they cannot use it again for the duration of the spell's cool down.

You have crafted a Belt that specializes in hurting your attackers when taking damage. While it does not wear down like what Thorn Enchantment does to armor, it does use the wearer's Soul Energy when doing this. It can be enchanted with Thorns to increase damage.

The Soul Shield Amulet mimics the Wither's shield when its power has ebbed. Should its wearer be half or less of their maximum health, arrows will bounced off them. Should one be capable of Creative Flight without being in Creative, they will find themselves grounded when the shield is up.

A variant of the Wind Robes that takes the very lightning in its fabrics. Much like the Wind Robes, the robes allows you to fall slowly. Wearing the Robes also halves the Soul Cost for Storm Spells, but not Wind Spells unfortunately.
Creatures of the storms slowly heal themselves with their summoner's soul energy, should they wear this robe.
The Storm Crown reduce the amount of time to cast Storm spells by half and keeps your storm servants from dying off like Vexes.

Trying to hit your foes with your spells can be an ordeal as they could avoid your Magical Fangs with but a single step. With this monocle, you can lock onto nearby foes by pressing the 'Activate Curio' key, allowing you to more accurately hit them with a spell.
Pressing the 'Activate Curio' key while active will change to another nearby foe. Pressing the key while crouching will deactivate the monocle.

Hammers are quite heavy for a dark wizard such as yourself. Fortunately, with your crafting and forging expertise, you've discovered a way to create a pair of gloves that helps you to wield Hammers more efficiently, increasing the attack speed by 50%%.

Using the $(l)purest$() blood of the dark emissary, $(l)which can only be obtained by slaying them within the Nether$(), you've made replica of their garments. The Robes gives you immunity to fire and Burn Hexes, and both robe and hat empowers some spells with hellfire.

The Unholy Hat reduces all incoming damage towards the wearer when within the Nether, as well as capping the configurable max amount of damage the wearer can take much like Apostles. The Unholy Robes grants resistance to hellfire damage.

The Void Robes imbues the wearer the power of the End. Wearers will have the chance of dodge attacks through teleportation, be immune to Void Touched and can move through Void Blocks freely. The Robes also makes Void Spells cheaper.

The Void Crown reduce the amount of time to cast Void spells by half and keeps certain void servants from dying off like Vexes. It also allows the wearer to gaze into Endermen without aggravating them.

Warlocks are known to have a very fungal brown robes with a nice sash wrapped around it. With some Red Wool, A couple of Wartful Eggs and Nether Warts, you've figured out how to make your own Warlock sash and which makes it so using that a Wartful Egg no longer harms you.

The Warlock Robe causes the wearer to be resistant to magic damage and provides a 10%% chance of not consuming any Wartful Eggs or a Snap Fungi and gives a 25%% chance for an additional Snap Fungi to drop from full grown Snap Warts. The Sash and Robe also cause Spiders to more likely drop Spider Eggs. If the wearer has a negative status effect, the garment will automatically use up any Wartful Eggs within the wearer's inventory.
Much like wearing a Witches Hat and Robe, wearing Warlock Robes causes all Witches and Warlocks to be neutral and barter-able.

The Wayfarer's Belt allows the wearer to not only move a bit faster, but also allows them to walk up a single block without jumping. The Belt also increases the jump height of the wearer and halves damage caused by falling off high places.

The Wild Robes allows you to harness the power of nature far more efficiently and effectively. Servants that spews poison, for instance, will instead give Acid Venom, which affects even the Undead. Consequently, the Robes also provides immunity to poison and said venom!
Creatures born from Wild magic can slowly heal themselves using their summoner's soul energy, should the summoner don this robe.
The Wild Crown reduce the amount of time to cast Wild spells by half and keeps your wild servants from dying off like Vexes.

The Wind Robes allows you to fall slowly(or not so slowly when holding shift) and make you immune to fall damage. However, every second the robes slow your fall, Soul Energy is consumed. Wearing the Robes also halves the Soul Cost for Wind Spells.
The creatures of the winds can use their summoner's soul energy to slowly heal themselves, should they wear this robe.
The jade crown will halved the time to cast Wind spells and keeps your wind servants from dying off, like Vexes, when worn.

Witches are known to look snazzy with their massive hats. You've figured out how to make your own Witch hat with some Dark Fabrics and you've discovered how wearing them gives you a small chance of not consuming any potion.

You've also discovered a way to replicate the powers of a Witch by crafting your own Witches Robes. The Robe is essentially a portable Brewing Stand (that you can open by pressing the default key: V while wearing it). It also provides resistance to magical attacks.

Wearing a Witches Hat while wearing the Witches Robes not only makes the robe brew potions faster, but also makes Witches and Warlocks neutral to the wearer. You can also barter with Witches and Warlocks by right-clicking on them with an Emerald, but only if they're not aggressive or holding something. Unlike the brutish Piglins, the two won't pick up Emeralds thrown at them, you gotta give it to them straight.
The Abyss Staff gives the wielder great authority over the waves, increasing the power of Abyss Spells.
Through the freezing cold of the Frost Staff, the power of Frost Spells is heightened.
While Geomancers use simple wooden canes to power their geomancy, you've know you can do better with the Amethysts you have lying around.
The Geo Staff empowers up several Geomancy spells, granting more power over the very earth itself!
With the forbidden texts, you have discovered a way to harness the power of the night, allowing you to create a powerful staff that bring you supremacy in necromancy.

$(l:focuses/soul_bolt_focus)Soul Bolts$() shot from this staff will turn into the more powerful Necro Bolts. Casting the $(l:focuses/illusion_focus)Mirror Spell$() while also wearing the $(l:crafts/garment/nameless_set)Nameless Set$() will cause them to shoot a single Necro Bolt at your target instead.

The Ectoplasms dropped by the Wraiths gave you an idea. With some $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingots$(), you've managed to create an upgrade to your $(l:intro/dark_wand)Wand$() and create a Staff fit for a Necromancer.
The Necro Staff powers up Necroturgic spells, allowing one to summon more than 1 Undead Servant per cast for example.
After learning the powers of the Wither Necromancers, you're able to replicate their staff, empowering your Nether spells.
After killing those high ranking $(l:world/bestiary/minister)illagers$(), you've managed to procure their powerful orb and use it to make a replica of their staff.
The Ominous Staff powers up certain magical spells. Vexing, Biting, Feasting, Shredding and Teeth spells to be precise. Casting Rotting and Osseous spells summons undead illagers instead.
The power of the storms and lightning rest within this staff. With it, storm spells are no longer affected by Lightning Rods and can chain lightning multiple non-allied mobs.
With the void and the End whirling around this eldritch staff, your Void Spells become more greater.
The natural world can be hard to tame, but with some dark magic and wood, you've crafted a staff that heightens the natural and unnatural powers of Wild spells.

You've learned tales of a sanctum and their control and experimentation of winds and how they can control it to an extant through their staffs. After some research and experimentation, you've discovered a way to replicate their ancient staffs.
The Wind Staff obviously powers up Wind spells, granting greater control over the winds themselves.

Cursed Metal Ingots seems to have the same properties as regular Iron Ingots, making it redundant to make an armor set based on it. However, with some tinkering, the ingots can be used to upgrade the regular Iron Armor to something better.

Not only does it provide toughness, but each piece somewhat mitigates magic, fire and explosive damage. Each pieces also provides a discount on using Soul Energy, whether it's used to cast spells, heal servants and repairing certain items. It doesn't discount usage in crafting or rituals unfortunately. Wearing allows summons to grant Soul Energy when they kill a mob.
Inspired by your foe, you've crafted a blade using the powers of the void and added some Dark Alloy to grant it the ability to self-repair with Soul Energy.

The blade allows one to charge at a direction by right-clicking while sprinting, or to back step away by right-clicking without sprinting, though it will cause the blade to enter cooldown. The blade causes Void Touched and is sharp enough to send a void-powered razor wind when swung at full power, when it's not cooling down.
It can be repaired with Netherite Ingots on an anvil.

$(o)When crafting this blade, the energies gave you visions, of what looks to be the past, of people crafting some artifacts, one of which looks to be sword, another an orb. You see the sword being used many times, with many wielders... until it might as well wield itself. You see someone, or something, putting the orb inside a crystal... and turn into something else.$()
Fashioned in the likeness of a skull, this hammer pull nearby creatures towards the target of impact when swung at full power.
It can perform the same functionalities as it's mundane counterpart. The hammer can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingot$().

While Dark Alloy can be used to craft regular tools, when it comes to armor, it seems to require more... elaborate ways of crafting them. The armor looks nothing like the others you have crafted, looking more elaborate yet intimidating, but it still provides Diamond level protection and toughness, as well as some knockback resistance.
Much like the Black Iron Armor set, the armor also provides discount on Soul Energy, but also slightly mitigates magic, fire and explosive damage.

The Death Scythe is the most powerful of its kind, with blades so sharp that its slashes not only can travel through the air, hitting beings far from its wielder, but also makes them more vulnerable. It repairs itself using the wielder's Soul Energy.

The Eerie Pickaxe is a powerful tool that allows the user to reach 3 Blocks further. Breaking a block with this Pickaxe will cause the content to immediately transfer towards the user as well as any nearby experience orbs. However, there's a reason why the Pickaxe has been named Eerie...
The pickaxe can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingot$().
The Fanged Dagger might not seem impressive, but provides high attack speed compared to Swords and poisons targets. When a creature is killed, the bearer gains more Soul Energy than before.
The dagger can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingot$(). Added from pantman687's suggestion

A Shovel suited for gravediggers and grave robbers, the shovel breaks 2 blocks instead of one when breaking a blocks like dirt, allowing the user to dig up graves on the fly. The reason for its name is how the shovel has a 10%% chance of digging up remains when breaking blocks like dirt or sand.
The shovel can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingot$().

Blacksmiths and soldiers alike use the Great Hammer for its strength in forging and in battle. If the wielder's attack recharge meter is full, the hammer will hit beings at a great radius though it will take quite a while for the meter to recover which can be mitigated if the wielder doesn't hold anything offhand.

The hammer can mine a 3x3 area, but have less mining speed than pickaxes. As the hammer is use for forging, right-clicking a Block of Iron with it will turn it into a heavily damaged Anvil. The hammer can be repaired on an anvil with an Iron Ingot.
Legends spoke of witches riding on brooms and fly off into the sky. After some research, you've figured out a way to make one for yourself.

The Haunted Broom is essentially a Wand deprived of being able to cast spells, but given the strength and ability to carry you through the air. The broom only respond to forward inputs, and will fly towards the direction you are looking at, though you would need to look behind you to slow down. Careful not to fly to quickly, as crashing upon a solid block can cause you to take damage and for your broom to break, upon impact.

Unfortunately, there's a cost. For every 8 blocks, by default, vertically or horizontally, the broom needs to feed off their rider's Soul Energy. If deprived the amount of Soul Energy needed to fly, the broom will break, dropping you and the broom from the sky. If you have an insufficient amount of Soul Energy, you'll be unable to ride on Haunted Broom.

Haunted Brooms have their own unique enchantments. Hardy makes them less likely to break and Fealty will cause them to return back to their placer when broken as well as prevent others from using it once placed after getting the enchantment.
pages.title: Broom Enchantments

pages.text: Haunted Brooms can surprisingly be enchanted with two $(l:focuses/focus_enchantments)focus enchantments$(). Velocity will, of course, increase the speed of the broom. Burning, however, has a special effect in that if a broom were to break upon collision with a solid block, it will explode! The size of which depends on how fast the broom was going.

According to some of your research, the brooms were actually the witch's staff disguised with a brush on it. Also, they most likely rode it the with the brush at the front, but it seems to me an old and outdated trend in this world.
A version of the Fanged Dagger that, while no longer venomous, will heal the wielder 5%% of damage dealt by it. The lifesteal percentage increases with each Soul Eater enchantment level.
The dagger can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:crafts/dark_alloy_ingot)Dark Alloy Ingot$(), though it will self repair if the wielder has Soul Energy.
A Bow suited to killing game, any animal slain by an arrow shot from this bow will drop more loot than even a Looting III weapon.
The bow can be repaired on an anvil when combined with any bow.
These pickaxe looking axes are useful at collecting ice and pushing you up over obstacles, though they lack the shield-disabling and wood-stripping abilities of true axes.
Heretics have a chance of dropping or bartering an Infernal Tome, which can be read to replicate their hellish chants but will burn and nauseate those unworthy of the Nether's gifts when doing so...
The Infernal Tome can be repaired with paper on an Anvil (Don't ask why an Anvil is used to repair books...).

The Ominous Scythe is a powerful weapon capable of hitting multiple beings per hit. Not only does it hit hard, but the wielder gains Soul Energy with each hit. If the wielder's attack recharge meter is full, the scythe will hit beings at a higher radius though it will take quite a while for the meter to recover which can be mitigated if the wielder doesn't hold anything offhand.

The scythe can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingot$() or a $(l:crafts/pale_steel_ingot)Pale Steel Ingot$(). It can also be used as a tool to clear out grass or harvest crops in a large area or to collect Sculk blocks without Silk Touch.
An upgraded version of the Ominous Scythe, possessing the qualities of other $(l:crafts/dark_alloy_ingot)Dark Alloy$() equipment.

The Philosopher's Mace is the ultimate weapon/tool as not only can it smash enemies into pieces, but it can also mine blocks like a pickaxe or a shovel. When a target is struck with the mace, they gained Gold Touch effect, which causes them to drop Gold Nuggets upon death.
The Netherite used to forge this weapon/tool made the mace fire-resistant and prevents it from being destroyed when in fire or lava.

An axe that hungers for both Blood and Wood. When killing a creature or chopping down wood, the user becomes slightly stronger and their hands move quicker for 10 seconds. Continuous killings/choppings amplifies the effect. Should the user amplify the effect 5 times, the result has been described as 'explosive'.
The axe can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:intro/magical_components)Cursed Metal Ingot$().
The Stormlander, enchanted with the power of the raging storm, is a treasure of the Illagers.
It can perform the same functionalities as it's mundane counterpart. The hammer can be repaired on an anvil with a $(l:crafts/pale_steel_ingot)Pale Steel Ingot$().

Summoning golems and constructs using an $(l:crafts/cores)Animation Core$() can be such a tedious task, especially when done constantly. After some research and experiments, you've managed to create a device that can animate golems for you.

The Animator not only requires to be placed atop of a filled $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$(), it also requires a bound $(l:crafts/waystone)Waystone$() placed in it. Animating a golem or construct requires soul energy, with the amount depending on how far the bound location is towards the Animator. The bound location should be where the summoner would've used an Animation Core at to summon a golem. A redstone signal is needed to activate the machine, provided that both requirements were reached.

The Waystone are placed in the machine the same way Totems are placed into Cursed Cages. Looking at a filled Animator while crouching will show the co-ordinates, owner and soul energy requirement. Right-clicking on it with an empty hand and while crouching will visualize the bound location.
The Apparition Door is a device that will turn intangible when right-clicked or activated through redstone. The door also trigger other adjacent doors to do the same.

After some research, you've found a way to create a more powerful and versatile version of the $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$(). The Arca will store and distribute your Soul Energy making it so you won't need to use or carry a Totem of Souls anymore.
The Arca is one of the toughest blocks you have encountered, with the preservation of water and extra Obsidian, it's strength and Explosive Resistance is beyond most materials besides Bedrock.

When you place down an Arca, the Arca will see you as its owner. As the owner, you can instantly break your Arca by right-clicking on it while crouching, which is quite handy considering how hard it is. Also, the Arca now holds all Soul Energy the owner collects and use, and will override any Totem of Souls the Owner has.
Due to this, one should use $(l:crafts/soul_transfer_gem)Transfer Gems$() to power one's Cursed Cages as trying to fill up a Totem with an Arca can be a tricky process.
Runes shows which Arca is being used.

You can only have ONE Arca, placing another will cause the new Arca to replace the former. If the Arca is broken, the Soul Energy stored within will slowly evaporate, causing Soul Hunger, which weakens and slows you down, until all the Energy is gone or another Arca is placed. If there are multiple Arcas, right clicking an unused one with an empty hand will transfer which Arca is being used.

You can adjust where the Arca will place you down when saving you from death. Right-click on the Arca with a Waystone, that has recorded a position within 8 blocks from the Arca, and it will try to revive you at that location instead of near itself.

A soul-hungering crystal that, when placed down, will link itself to you and will attempt to suck in soul energy from any nearby entity, that's not allied to you, damaging them until they are at low health.
While you're unable to recreate the Blaze Spawners found in Fortresses, you've managed to figure out a way to create a simulacrum that properly produces a loyal Blaze, though with a price.

The cage requires a Magma Block to be added, in order to call forth a Blaze Servant. Much like the Spider Nest, right-clicking the nest with a Wand or Staff will make it so that it will only spawn a servant if a valid target is near it. While crouching, however, it will change whether the servant will spawn guarding the block or following the owner.
Crystal Balls are known to be used for scrying or to foresee the future.

Using a filled $(l:crafts/waystone)Waystone$() on it will cause you to look upon the location from above, provided that said location is loaded. Using a filled $(l:crafts/taglock_kit)Taglock Kit$() on it will cause you to look through the victim's eyes, provided said victim is either the same creature as you, or if the victim is within 80 blocks from you or one of your kind.

Either method requires the location or victim to be on the same dimension, and be within 1024 blocks from the ball, though there are $(l:world/blighted_shacks)rumors$() of a crystal ball that does not have that specific restriction...
Anvils can be very annoying to deal with. Not only can they break, they also demand a lot, and have a limit of, experience they can take. With Dark Alloy, you are able to create a much better Anvil.

The Dark Anvil can repair itself when placed on top of a $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$(), where it would uncommonly take a large amount of Soul Energy from it to mend itself. Using the Dark Anvil does not multiply the repair cost of the item by 2, but will add by 1. Instead of preventing you from repairing/enchanting items if the level cost is too high, the cost will stay at the level limit, allowing the item to be used on the anvil regardless.
A Redstone Lamp infused with never-ending frost, that slowly freezes the area around itself. When powered, the lamp turns off and stops working.

With ectoplasms, you've created a glass that's only intangible to you and your fellows, allowing you all to pass through it like air. Creatures and items cannot pass through, and the glass can be tinted to prevent even light to pass.
You can also invert the glass' functionality, making everything but you and your fellows from passing.
Sometimes a dark wizard needs more than just two water source blocks to obtain infinite water, something more compact and manageable perhaps.

The Haunted Jug holds infinite supply of water that anyone can take through buckets, bottles and even pipes! However, what truly makes this jug special is that, as it's name suggests, is that it's haunted with spiritual energies.
The jug will attempt to fill in any nearby valid container, such as cauldrons, with water, and will even extinguish any creature that's lit aflame near itself.
Right-clicking on the jug with a Wand/Staff will put a lid on it, disabling the feature, or remove it if it's lidded.
With some studies and experimentation, you've discovered a way to transform a piece of Haunted Glass into a mirror that allows you to essentially teleport from one place to another.

In order to teleport by using Mirrors, you must have two placed down in the world on the same X and Z or Y-Axis. For the X and Z, or horizontal axis, two mirrors must be placed on the same Y axis, each facing way from each other, within 32 blocks, making it seem like a tunnel or hole between walls.

For a the Y, or vertical, axis, the Mirrors must be facing the same way, and share the same XZ coordinates, either 16 blocks below or above each other. Mirrors will attempt to find another mirror above itself before searching below.

When dealing with Raids, some of the Raiders have a bad tendency of falling into holes, appearing in places deep underground and so on. After many research, you've managed to improve on the Villager's Bell to not only have a much higher radius of effect, but also teleports any Raider towards the Bell's vicinity if they're more than 16 Blocks away from it!
Unfortunately, the newly Hook Bell does not respond to any Redstone power and can only be rung, by hand or from projectiles shot, from beings like yourself.

With the ectoplasm dropped by those Wraiths, you are able to harness their mystical unflames into a machine that will burn any living creature on it. The unflames seems to sap Soul Energy when burning the creature above, the Activated Emerald allows the energy to transfer towards the block's placer.
The machine will activate with a redstone signal. The fire doesn't hurt the placer.

The Deep Dark holds a lot of Necrotic energies, as evidence by the abundance of Sculk that doted the underbiome. By infusing a Shade Brazier with Necrotic elements, you've created a device that can channel the dark energies of the biome to create all kinds of items.

Necrotic Brazier burns with a green flame that seems to not harm the Undead, and can only burn if placed within the Deep Dark. The Brazier takes in multiple items to craft one, and the items can either be placed by hand or dropped on top of it. It will not accept any items dropped on to it if it's in the process of crafting.

The Necrotic Brazier will slowly take Soul Energy from the surrounding $(l:crafts/artifice/soul_candlestick)Soul Candlesticks$(), only completing, and spewing out the resulting item, once it has taken enough consuming all the items placed in it. Breaking every $(l:crafts/artifice/soul_candlestick)Candlesticks$(), not having enough Soul Energy from them, or attempting to place or remove an item from the Brazier will cause it to spit out all of its items, wasting any consumed Soul Energy.
The Night Beacon is an ancient device told within Villager Legends. They say that the Piglins placed it upon a Nether Portal, where it caused the Overworld to be in perpetual night.
But the legends spoke of its destruction. Perhaps what you have obtained was a replica of such arcane device, one that much like the legends of old, can bring eternal night upon the world.
Handling a large amount of Servants can be a hassle, so you've created a special Wall Shrine that tells your Servants to guard a specific area when they go near it.

There are multiple ways to record the location and what type of servant would be affected by it. One is by simply shift right-click the block you want your servants to go to with the decree itself and to 'hit' your servant to record its type. The second way is by placing down the decree to a wall, and right-click on it with a recorded Waystone for the location, or a filled Taglock Kit to record the type it only effects (the type must be of a servant). It does not affect servants that are $(l:goety:crafts/grimoire_of_grounding)grounded$().

Right-clicking on a placed down decree without pressing shift, or right-clicking the air with it on main hand, will cause it to enter into one out of three modes, cycling through them. The first mode affects servants of all ages, the second only affects baby servants, the third only adult servants and then back to the first mode. When right-clicking on it with a Wand/Staff however, the range of the decree's influence can be adjusted, increasing the range up to 8 blocks, or decreasing it down to 1 if shift-right clicking, at all directions. Shift-right clicking without a wand/staff, taglock kits, or waystones will show the linked location and influence range of the decree.

The decree can record the location of an Ominous Pyre, which can lead to special interactions with $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)Neollagers$(). If the Pyre is lit, the Neollagers commanded to the Pyre will train if possible. It also distinguishes the type of Neollager it commands to train, as if the Pyre is training to a non-magic role, it will not command the magically inclined Neollagers to train at it and it will not command those without magic if the pyre does train a magic role.

The decree also have other special interactions with raiding servants, but only if said servants are not following a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants#captain)captain$(). The decree can record $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants#chest)chests$() and $(l:goety:crafts/artifice/ominous_idol)idols$() for Illagers and other Raiders to link to, but only if they're aren't link to any in the first place. When linking, the raider will not be commanded or order to guard the linked location.
A sinister statue that can save the lives of illagers and similar ilk that are bound to it.

Rather than dying, those bound to the idol will teleport back to it at the precipice of death, unless it was by their master dismissing them with a Wand/Staff, or if the idol they're bound with is in another dimension. They will, however, be grievously wounded, unable to be revived for a Minecraft day, and be crippled for 5 minutes until they are sufficiently healed.

To bind your servant to the idol, simply use a Waystone, have it bound to the statue, and right click your servant with it. The idol can only hold up to 16 servants (by default) and will not accept more after. Much like other artifices, the idol requires Soul Energy to function, which it gets by placing it on top of a filled $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$().

The pyre inspires loyal $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)Neollagers$() to train themselves. To have the Neollager train at a pyre, simply $(l:goety:focuses/command_focus)Command$() / $(l:goety:focuses/order_focus)Order$() them to it. If 'illagerServantAutoTrain' is enabled, simply have them near one. Depending on its surroundings, much like $(l:rituals/dark_altar)Altars$(), will allow the Neollager to train into a specific Illager subtype. Each pyre can only train up to 8 Trainable Illagers.

pages.text: To stop them from training, either remove the Pyre or move them more than 10 blocks away from it. If a training Illager is near Illagers they're training to become, they will train faster.

A mystical block that powers up when strong winds are blown upon it, much like ones made by $(l:goety:crafts/artifice/wind_blower)Wind Blowers$(). The crystal can store $(l:goety:summons/squall_golem)Squall Golems$() upon itself, when left-clicking it on one, and will activate them once powered.

Not only can they power Squall Golems, they can also power other Resonance Crystals as well. Right-clicking on one with a $(l:goety:crafts/waystone)Waystone$() that has registered a location that has a different crystal will have it store the location. It will not use up the waystone and can store multiple crystal locations at once, but only if said crystal is less, or equal to, 64 blocks from it.

If it has stored any locations, right-clicking on the crystal with an empty hand will show the positions it's connected to, shift-right clicking, however, will remove all positions from the crystal. Breaking the crystal will also remove all recorded locations. When active, it emits Redstone power.

The Sculk Catalyst converts the dead into Sculk but it seems to devour the Soul Energies of the creature to convert them. With the use of the Soul Absorber, you are able to make the Catalyst absorb Soul Energy from the $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$() and spread Sculk around it.
The Sculk Converter requires a Redstone Signal to absorb Soul Energy and spread Sculk.

The Sculk Converter can also be enchanted with Potency, which will cause it to absorb more Soul Energy and spread more Sculk. It appears your tinkering with this odd object causes it to stop spreading Sculk when a creature nearby dies.

The Sculk Catalyst is a fascinating thing. It converts Experience into Sculk which spreads across the world, but with some tinkering, you've managed to turn the Catalyst into a Soul Energy collector that converts Experience straight to Soul Energy.

The amount of Soul Energy delivered is the same amount as the experience dropped. The Devourer can be enchanted with Soul Eater and Radius. Radius multiplies the area of which Experience is absorbed, ie, Radius I doubles the area, Radius II triples. Soul Eater multiplies the amount of Soul Energy gathered from Experience.
With the way the Sculk grows using Soul Energy, you wonder if you can use it to grow crops instead of more of itself. Enter the Sculk Grower.

The Sculk Grower requires a $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$() on top of it, much like the Sculk Converter. Unlike the Sculk Converter, it will remain active with a constant Redstone signal, and it absorbs Soul Energy in bulk rather than slowly siphoning it. When it absorbs a bulk of Soul Energy, it gains 'Charges' which is used to speed up the growth of the surrounding crops.

Usually, the Sculk Grower grows random crops from a 8 x 4 x 8 Blocks around it, but the Grower can be enchanted with Radius (Though, unlike, say, the Sculk Devourer, the Radius adds rather than multiply). If not supplied with Redstone, the Grower will still grow crops until it runs out of Charges. If there aren't any crops around the Grower(Or the Continuous Growth Config is disabled), its Charges will decay within itself.

The Sculk Converter can be a messy contraption, as it spreads Sculk around itself. With this Relay, the Converter will instead spread Sculk around the Relay's location instead! Right clicking on the Converter with an empty hand will show the Relay it's using. The Relay can be harvested with a Silk-Touched Hoe.
The Sculk Converter will only use the closest Relay.

Shade stone and cursed metal are great at funneling necrotic energies. With some tinkering and the Rotting Focus, you've managed to create a special gravestone that can summon forth loyal Zombie Servants on demand.

The gravestone requires an Iron Nugget to be added, in order to call forth a Zombie Servant. Much like the Spider Nest, right-clicking the nest with a Wand or Staff will make it so that it will only spawn a servant if a valid target is near it. While crouching, however, it will change whether the servant will spawn guarding the block or following the owner.
Depending on its surroundings, much like $(l:rituals/dark_altar)Altars$(), the servant can spawn as a different variant from a regular Zombie.

pages.text: The illagers are persistent with hunting down those who have delved into the dark arts. With a bunch of their skulls and a shrieker from the dark, you've found a way to remind them of their place.
The Shrieking Obelisk lets out a fearful shriek that wards off any illagers that tries to launch an assault upon you. It requires to be placed on top of a filled Cursed Cage to be active.
Up to 4 levels of skulls can be placed.
pages.name: Placement Example

pages.text: Tall Skulls placed around the Obelisk, like the blocks around a Beacon, though only on the outlines, will increase the Shrieking Obelisk's radius of effect.

With the $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$(), you wonder what you should do with your old Totem of Souls. Stashing it away is an option, but you wondered if you can somehow transfer all the Soul Energy within it towards your Arca.

With the Soul Absorber, you are able to siphon the Soul Energies from not only your Totem of Souls but other items such as the Evokers' Totems and Soul Sand to put within your $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$(). While the Soul Absorber will slowly drain Totem of Souls, other items will simply burn up and disappear once it has absorbed its Soul Energy.

Certain devices require a large portion of Soul Energy, but are unable to directly take the energy from the $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$(). After some experiments, you've discovered a way to have such devices siphon energies from multiple Cursed Cages instead of one. Such devices usually process faster the more Candlesticks and filled Cages are, usually usually 8 blocks, around it.
Placed one on top of a filled $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$().

The Soul Menderer is a powerful device that repairs damaged weapons and tools using Soul Energy. The Soul Menderer must be placed on-top of a $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$() with a Totem or $(l:crafts/soul_transfer_gem)Transfer Gem$() in it to activate, then it will slowly repair the item within itself.

With a bunch of Spider Eggs surrounding a piece of raw meat allows you to create a Spider Nest. Right-clicking on it, or using a hopper, with meat will cause it to produce a loyal $(l:summons/spider_servants)Spider Servant$(). Depending on its surroundings, much like $(l:rituals/dark_altar)Altars$(), the servant can spawn as a different variant from a regular spider.

Right-clicking the nest with a Wand or Staff will make it so that it will only spawn a servant if a valid target is near it. While crouching, however, it will change whether the servant will spawn guarding the block or following the owner.
