pages.text: The power of the Wind Core allows for the creation of powerful blowers, that pushes all but the sturdious of creatures in front of it. Crouching will reduce the push on you, allowing you to go against the wind. The power of the blower is based on the redstone power it receives, the higher, the stronger.
Requirements: $(li)Be in the Nether $(li)8 Basalts Any $(li)16 Blackstone Any $(li)4 Glowstone
An example of how the ritual can be placed.

The Nether is a dimension full of Soul Energy, as shown with the endless amounts of Soul Sand that littered the realm. However, there still needs structure to create Nether related artifacts to focus the abundance into one place. The Blackstone and Basalt can be of any kind.
Requirements: $(li)15 Ladders $(li)15 Rails $(li)1 Carved Pumpkin
An example of how the ritual can be placed.

From your studies, you figured out a way to make rituals that surrounds summoning and controlling creatures. The rails and ladders are to signify motion, and the pumpkin signifies life, for a Carved Pumpkin is what gives life to Snow and Iron. Funnily, through your researches, you've found out that aside from giving life, pumpkins also have a magical property that stops Enderman from being enraged if you stare at them while wearing it, and not because you are fooling them.

The Dark Altar is the centerpiece of most Rituals. Before anything, the Altar must be placed above a $(l:intro/cursed_cage)Cursed Cage$(), and the Cage must have Soul Energy for the Altar to function.

By using a Dark Altar, you may craft a certain item or summon a creature depending on the blocks and items surrounding the Altar. Unlike other schools of magic, these blocks do $(l)not$() need to be arranged in a certain order for the ritual to function. What matters is the certain amount of certain blocks are $(l)within$() the Altar's $(l)8, by default, block radius.$() Shift right-clicking on the Dark Altar with an empty hand will show the range of affect, doing it again will hide it.

To begin the ritual, you must filled the pedestals first with the required items $(l)before$() placing the Altar's item. When the ritual is ongoing, the Altar will siphon Soul Energy from the Cage, so you best make sure it has enough of it before enacting a Ritual! The Pedestals can be used for decoration.
Requirements: $(li)Altar is in Deep Ocean biome and below sea level $(br)$(l)OR$()$() $(li)4 Sea Lanterns $(li)16 Prismarine Blocks Any $(li)16 Granite Blocks Any $(br)Altar must be waterlogged$()
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
The power of the ocean courses through the Altar, allowing you harness the very tides for your own diabolical purposes.
Requirements: $(li)1 Crystal Ball Any $(li)16 Lit Candles $(li)1 Skeleton Skull
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
The word 'Necromancy' refers to the art of divination through spirits of the dead. Using the power of souls, you are able to perform rituals that can reveal locations of certain areas to you.
The Dark Altar can enchant items using certain ingredients, soul energy, and the ritual caster's own experience levels.

The rituals can enchant even enchanted items, so long as the item's enchantments are compatible with the enchantment, and can increase the level enchantment as well. However, when increasing the enchantment level, the experience level required is doubled.
Requirements: $(li)Be in the End $(li)16 Void Blocks $(li)64 End Stone Variants $(li)32 Purpur Blocks Any
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
The concentrated essence of the Void helps channel the powers of the end of all things into making arcane rituals.
Requirements: $(li)Be in the Nether $(li)4 Wither Skeleton Skulls $(li)32 Nether/Red Nether Bricks $(li)8 Nether Warts
An example of how the ritual can be placed.

The Wither Skeletons are the charred remains of the Fortress' original inhabitants, ones Nether Cultists called 'Nephilim', betrayed by their own flaming creations. Even in death, they still hold magical power, and perhaps even retained some arcane knowledge for advanced magics. Perhaps the Warts growing from the anguish of the damned also holds some of its victims' knowledge as well.
Requirements: $(li)1 Cauldron full of Lava $(li)2 Furnaces or Blast Furnaces $(li)1 Anvils
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
Creating a Forge around the Dark Altar allows you to craft certain items and upgrade your magical arsenal.
Requirements: $(li)Altar is located in a snowing biome $(br)$(l)OR$()$() $(li)16 Ice Blocks of any type $(li)8 Snow Blocks $(li)4 $(l:goety:crafts/artifice/freezing_lamp)Freezing Lamps$()
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
Surrounding the Altar with freezing bricks and blocks allows it to use the cold to craft all kinds of magic.
Requirements: $(li)Altar is at or below 32 height, not expose to sky $(br)$(l)OR$()$() $(li)1 Smithing Table $(li)8 Blocks of Amethyst $(li)16 Deepslate Blocks
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
Placing the Altar deep beneath and surrounding it with deepslate and amethysts, you will be able to harness the earth to create all kinds of jewels and magics.
Requirements: $(li)16 Bookshelves/Enchant Power $(li)1 Enchanting Table $(li)1 Lectern with Book
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
Surrounding the Altar with large quantities of books will help create certain Magical Items.
Requirements: $(li)16 Non-Wooden Slabs $(li)16 Sculk Blocks or $(l:goety:crafts/grave_soil)Grave Soils$() $(li)8 Non-Empty Flower Pots $(li)Must be done at Night
An example of how the ritual can be placed.

By constructing graves with either Sculk or Grave Soils, you found a way to gather up more necroturgic energies to use for Rituals. However, while Sculk holds a vast amount of necrotic energy, Grave Soil is more fragile, and have a large chance of being turned into Dark Dirt once a ritual is finished.
Requirements: $(li)Altar is in Jungle biome $(br)$(l)OR$()$() $(li)32 Leaves Any $(li)16 Overgrown Roots $(li)16 Mossy Blocks Any
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
The wild powers of nature, growth and life can be channeled and perverted through this ritual for dark ends.
Requirements: $(li)8 Crying Obsidian $(li)16 Obsidian $(li)4 Soul Fires
An example of how the ritual can be placed.

You've heard rumors of a powerful being that lurks within the Nether. Rumor has it that a cabal of Nether Cultists met with what a being they called an 'Apostle' in a circle of Obsidian where they appeared before them and told them secrets.

Perhaps, with some trickery, magic and a baiting material, you are capable of summoning one for your own purposes, though you shouldn't summon one within the Nether where they're at their most powerful. (Recommended Equipment: Enchanted Armor, Smite Weapons and Efficiency Pickaxe)
Requirements: $(li)Altar at equal or above 128 Blocks height $(br)$(l)OR$()$() $(li)8 Marble Blocks $(li)16 Jade Tiles $(li)4 Indented Gold Blocks
An example of how the ritual can be placed if placed below height level.
By putting the Altar high in the air, you can harness the very winds and the sky to power your magics.
Requirements: $(li)Same as Sky Ritual $(li)Altar must be exposed to a Storm $(li)4 Lightning Rods $(li)20 Chains $(li)12 Copper Block Any.
An example of how the ritual can be placed.
The power of the storm will power your magical skills like no other! The Copper Blocks can be of any kind.
With $(l:crafts/waystone)Waystones$(), you're able to teleport to areas using Rituals, provided the area is within the same dimension.

Going through the dark arts, one will encounter all kinds of magical artifices that require Soul Energy to power. The Cursed Cage helps send Soul Energy to these devices, provided it has a Totem or some connection to a Soul Energy holder inserted in it.
You've also discovered a new enchantment: Soul Eater. Any weapon or tool enchanted with this, will increase the amount of Soul Energy gain when slaying a creature with it.
pages.title: Soul Eater

pages.text: While crafting using your Totem is all well and good, some of the items can demand a lot of resources, so you wondered if there's a way to obtain these items more cheaply. Throughout your research, you find that Lapis Lazulis can be used to create some sort of siphon. A way to attract some sort of magical energy towards it.

With some experiments and research, you've came up with the idea of a device, called a 'Cursed Infuser'. This device will siphon up magical energies from below it and infuse whatever items is place on it. While there are certain objects that hold some magical energies, there's one that seems to have an endless amount of it. Spawners.

By placing the Cursed Infuser atop of a Spawner, it will start to siphon the Spawner's energy and infuse certain items with it. You've no clue what fuels these monstrous machines, but perhaps the infuser will provide some clues.

It seems magical beings, like Evokers, cast spells by chanting and waving. They seemed to know how to cast these spells by heart through long studies and rituals. Fortunately, you've found a way to cast spells without prolong study by using a wand.
Using the newly discovered Magic Fabrics, you are able to use Soul Energy to cast spells.

However, the wand needs a $(l:focuses)Focus$() in order for a spell to be cast. Once the Focus is fitted in the wand, all the user must do is concentrate on the spell and have enough Soul Energy to cast a spell. To fit a Focus in the Wand, Press the Open Wand Focus Slot button (Default: Z) while holding the Wand and add the focus through your inventory. Having too many focuses might necessitate the creation of a $(l:crafts/garment/focus_bag)Focus Bag$(). To start making focuses, one must make an Empty Focus first.
Whether it be word of mouth, past experiences or stories, you have been very interested in what many have called, the 'Dark Arts'

The Dark Arts seems very different from the magics most people know. The most common magic available would be Enchanting. However, there's clearly more to magic than enchanting items. The act of summoning creatures to do one's bidding can be seen as a Dark Arts, for example. After all, most summonings you've encountered are done by foul forces.

Zombies seems to summon reinforcements out of nowhere, Evokers with Vexes, and the terrifying (but profitable) Spawners that are found in certain places in the world. With some scraps of knowledge you have an idea on accessing that those Spawners may be one of the keys to access these foul magics, or if they're too hard to find, some other way.

With your primitive Totem in hand, you've discovered that you can use it to craft brand new items that can be used to create all kinds of magical contraptions and focus! Though surely there's a more $(l:intro/cursed_infuser)cheaper way$() of getting these items...
The Evoker's Totem seems to have Emeralds placed where the eyes would be. You have a feeling that the Emeralds are different from the usual. Could there be a way to 'activate' them?
You've finally made a true simulacrum of the Evoker's Totem. This Totem can hold far more Soul Energy than the Totem of Roots.

Lapis Lazuli seems to be the main component for utilizing magic. Combining it with a bunch of strings creates a special string that channels magic better than its mundane counterpart. By combining these special strings with a dye or some other component, you're capable of creating special fabrics.

You have finally become the ultimate Undead. As you may have guessed, you have the strengths and weaknesses of Undeath. For starters, your hunger no longer goes up or down. When injured, you will use up the Soul Energy within your Totem to heal up all injuries (unless you're on fire).

Second, you cannot get the Poison, Regeneration, Hunger and/or Saturation effect. You will burn up in Sunlight unless you have something on your head and you gain more injuries from the Smite Enchantment. Also Villagers hate you unless you've cured a lot of them from being Zombies.

On the plus side, most Undead creatures no longer attack you, you can never drown and you can stay in the Sunlight all day long as you're wearing a Helmet or have Fire Resistance! Being Undead also means that Potions of Harming heals you while Potions of Healing harms you the same way as your Undead brethren.

$(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$() resurrections are initiated no matter the amount of Soul Energy is within it. However, should the number of Soul Energy be less that the usual number needed to revive you or that your Arca has been destroyed, you will lose your lichdom upon death.
You can also regain your living form by pressing the Lich Form key (Default: N). The form somehow does not fool anyone, but at least you have your former looks back.
You can also change the color of your Lich Form by right-clicking a Haunted Mirror with a dye. To remove the custom color, right-click the mirror with a bucket of water.
pages.title: Changing Colors

pages.text: You've researched on the secrets of the Illagers magic powers, Soul Energy, and you pondered on how to utilize and collect this energy.
With some twigs, an Ectoplasm and some Lapis Lazuli, you've managed to create your first Totem!

When killing a being with the Totem in the Hotbar or on a Charm Slot, it will fill up with Soul Energy. The amount depends on which creature is slain, but considering the Illagers disposition towards the Villagers, it's not hard to figure out which creature has the most amount of Soul Energy.

Soul Energy is what fuels their magic, and it seems to have a relation with Experience, though while Experience is used to enchant items and repair items if it has Mending, you've figure that Soul Energy can be used for more exotic purposes.
Loyal and aggressive, these bears make for fine servants to claw and rip apart your enemies. Also makes for a good mount, no saddle needed in fact, if you ignore its slow speed.
One can call upon a loyal bear through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/mauling_focus)Mauling Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Right-clicking on a loyal Bear Servant with fish will heal them. Summoning a bear servant on a cold biome or with a $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will call forth a Polar Bear Servant.
Another way of getting a Polar Bear Servant is to have a regular Polar Bear submit to you through a conversion ritual.
Bear Servants summoned through rituals can breed with each other when right-clicked with Honeycombs.
Thought to be fairy tales, these omens of death are very real and loyal to their summoner.
One can call upon a loyal black wolf through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Right-clicking on a loyal Black Wolf with meat will heal them.
Summoning Black Wolves through certain ways may also yield variants of the beast or even other types of hounds.

An undead version of regular wolves, though unlike them, these wolves may emit a howl that boosts the damage of their skeleton allies. Unlike the other two variants, these wolves don't turn invisible when hunting their query. They are summoned by casting $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting spell$() with a $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$(), or through another ritual.

These white furred canines are a terror to people living in cold areas, with their icy fangs and resistance to frost. They are summoned by casting $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting spell$() with a $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$(), summoned in snowing biomes, or through another ritual.

Legends of fiendish hounds that appear in a clap of thunder have been abound, now their lightning jaws are yours to command. They are summoned by casting $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting spell$() with a $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Storm Staff$(), summoned in an exposed storm, or through another ritual.

You've heard of tales and myths of hounds dragging the damned to the fires of the Nether, perhaps it's time to put these hounds to heel. They are summoned by casting $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting spell$() with a $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$(), summoned in Nether biomes, or through another ritual.

Based on the ancient vanguards, you've created a zombie variation that focuses on intimidation and brute force, rather than finesse. Wearing heavy plated armor and a spiked club, these undead horrors trade speed for strength and power.

If they're shield-less, right click on them with an Iron Ingot to give them their shield back when they're not attacking.$(br)One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/blackguard_focus)Blackguard Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.

What caused the Blazes to rebel against their makers? Deciphering the manuscript has shown what could be potential flaws but nothing concrete. In any case, you've found a way to make your own Blazes that would actually follow commands and defend their master.
Right-clicking on a loyal Blaze Servant with a Blaze Powder or Blaze Rod will heal them.

While a Vindicator can be raised as a Zombie, a Pillager a Skeleton, to truly make a proper undead version of the powerful Evokers and other Illager spellcasters, one must be more... spiritual in their pursuit.

Unlike the other two, Bound Evokers can float above ground and is unaffected by gravity. Despite their spiritual looks, they cannot phase through walls and can still be harmed with conventional weaponry.
No longer bound to the ground, these undead spellcasters nonetheless retain their mastery over the earth.
Bound Iceologers are as chilly as they are in life but, this time, their Ice Chunks are falling on someone else's head instead of yours.

As teary as they are in life, the undead Cryologers will rain hail and conjure walls upon their enemies. For some reason, despite their teary-eyed appearance, they seemed to be less miserable and more apathetic to their predicament than the other bound illagers.
These Illagers retain their power over the wind in death, with a neat caveat of truly being able to fly rather than slowly fall to the ground.
Not even death can stop the storm within these plunderers, and they're willing to reveal it to their foes.
These bound souls can be healed by right-clicking on them with Ectoplasm.

As they still retain their mental faculties, these souls can be given your $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants#banner)personal banner$() and lead your $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)Illager servants$() as well.
Some flies, when feeding upon the rotten flesh of the dead, can become enchanted with necrotic energies into becoming larger and ferocious.

Upon killing an creature, they spawn giant maggots, potentially more of them if the creature has high enough max health, that share their current lifespan if the have one, that will also turn into a Carrion Fly upon killing a creature. One can call upon a swarm of them through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/carrion_focus)Carrion Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.

They can, on harder difficulties, move through walls for some reason. Right-clicking on a loyal Carrion Fly with meat will heal them, though on Carrion Maggots, it will cause them to cocoon before they transform into a Carrion Fly.

Servants summoned by either Rituals or Spells tend to share some attributes with each other. For starters, they attack all kinds of Hostile Creatures, they won't attack each other if they share an Summoner, they have a limited lifespan and a limit on how many Servants a Summoner can have.

However, certain types of servants last forever if their summoner dons a associated crown and they can use their summoner's Soul Energy to heal themselves (provided they're not on fire) if said summoner wears the associated robe or, in the case of undead servants, Necro Cape. Undead Servants will burn in sunlight when not wearing a Helmet.

Servants can teleport to their Summoner if their summoner has their Focus equipped to their wands and cast the spell when crouching. If the summoned Servant is not a Vex, hitting them (or, if enabled through config, right click on them) with a $(l:intro/dark_wand)Wand$()/Staff will either make them follow the Summoner, wander around the area or stay put.
While similar to the clones conjured by Illusioners, these Doppelgangers will instead draw attention from hostile creatures and will disappear once hit or their summoner getting hit.
Their arrows do no damage to enemies and they will disappear after a certain amount of time.
Sub-species to Enderman, these odd creatures are far more sustainable to being bound to their summoner than their nigh impossible to control cousin.

All Enderlings are capable of teleportation, but unlike the Enderman, they don't teleport as often and some of them would disappear from combat for a couple of seconds to confuse their foes. They are also vulnerable to water.
Unfortunately, the book is incapable of showing their eyes properly for some arcane reason.
pages.name: Watchling Servant

pages.text: Watchling Servants are simple brutes that attack by teleporting in front of their enemy and swinging their arms at them. They can either be summoned through a ritual or casting with a $(l:focuses/void/watching_focus)Watching Focus$().

Blastling Servants are the toughest enderling health-wise, and attack by shooting a volley of hot goo at their enemies, though they would temporarily run or teleport away if a foe gets close to them. They can either be summoned through a ritual or casting with a $(l:focuses/void/blasting_focus)Blasting Focus$().

Snareling Servants are odd yet devious. They would first attempt at shooting their Snareling Goop at their foe, which would ensnare them for a time when hit, then they would either teleport or run towards their foe and attack them with their arms. They would temporarily try to run or teleport away if a foe gets close to them, if they're not ensnared. They can either be summoned through a ritual or casting with a $(l:focuses/void/snaring_focus)Snaring Focus$().
They can be healed by feeding them Chorus Fruits or wearing $(l:crafts/garment/void_robe)Void Robes with soul energy$().
The ancient texts have jotted down a method of creating a strange golem-like creature of flame and deepslate. The creature proves itself deadly with its flame breath and explosive jumps.
Right click the center Magma Block with an Animation Core.

The Brazier can be substituted with other types of decorative braziers, and the Deepslate can be substituted with other full blocks that have Deepslate in its name. They can be repaired by right-clicking on them with Magma Blocks or Furnace fuels. When it's hunkered down, right-clicking will cause it to rotate towards you, shift right-clicking will cause it to move to the center of the block it's on.

Sharks aren't as vicious as most would think and very rarely attack people on their own. These underwater fiends are another story, ripping and tearing up foes with their sharp teeth. Also makes for a good underwater mount without any need for a saddle.

One can call upon a loyal gnasher through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/mauling_focus)Mauling Focus$() underwater or through $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.

Right-clicking on a loyal Gnasher with fish will heal them. If the Gnasher was summoned through ritual, it can breed with another Gnasher summoned that way by right-clicking on them with meat while crouching.

With the schematics of an ancient war-machine and a way to possess Armor, you've got to thinking. After some trials and errors, you've discovered a way to create the ultimate Undead Servant: The Grave Golem.
Right click the center Skull Pile with an Animation Core.

The Stone Bricks can be substituted with other similar blocks such as Deepslate Bricks. The Golem has an assortment of abilities, from smashing its hands on the ground, shooting Haunted Skulls and summoning Haunts to aid it. The Golem can be commanded to follow, wander or stay in position through a wand/staff. They can be repaired by right-clicking on them with Bone Blocks or Bones, but can regenerate if the summoner wears a Necro Cape.

There's also another special ability the Golem possesses, should their Summoner die within 64 blocks near them, their items and equipment will be absorbed within the Golem. The Golem will glow reddish-orange to show that it has items contained itself. To get the items back, the Summoner simply needs to right-click on them with a Shovel. They'll also drop said items when killed. Of course, this requires the Summoner to actually drop their items upon death. (Suggested by JoTurtleGuy21)

Should the Golem fell from battle or command, they will drop their 'skull'. The Skull can be used to revive the Golem in a cheaper manner. However, the Skull remembers it's original creator and master and the revived Golem will only follow their commands.
These biomechanical cyclops are called from their monuments to serve under your command. While they do not need to breath to survive, it's best to not have them flail about on land.
One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/abyss/guardian_focus)Guardian Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Guardians can be healed by right-clicking on them with fishes.
Much like Vexes, Haunted Skulls can move through terrain but are more frailer and can only deal damage by exploding onto enemies. Their explosions don't effect their summoner nor their summons.
Hoglins make for fine servants to throw your enemies into the air with their mighty tusks. Also makes for a good mount, no saddle needed in fact, for some reason, if you ignore its slow speed.

But while loyal and brave, these Hoglins still retain their hatred of Warped Fungi and Nether Portals. They will also zombify outside of the Nether, turning the loyal creature into an omnicidal, and NOT loyal, Zoglin. One can call upon a loyal hoglin through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/mauling_focus)Mauling Focus$() while being in the Nether, or through a ritual which summons or converts one without a limited lifespan.
Right-clicking on a loyal Hoglin Servant with Crimson Roots or Weeping Vines will heal them.

Obtaining and wearing a $(l:crafts/garment/nether_robe)Nether Robes$() will stop the zombification from affecting your Hoglins. Using the $(l:focuses/wild/mauling_focus)Mauling Focus$() with a $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will call them forth no matter what dimension you're in.

A golem made of glacial frost and snow, they hold more power than Snow Golem, yet less power than Iron Golems. They attack by jabbing their foes with their ice spiked hands and rarely smash the ground and summon a $(l:focuses/frost/frost_nova_focus)frost nova$().
Right click the center Blue Ice with an Animation Core.

One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/frost/frostborn_focus)Frostborn Focus$(), or a permanent golem through this configuration. They can be healed by right-clicking on them with Ice, Packed Ice or Blue Ice.
A powerful ape-like creature made of roots and leaves, that can jump high and smash hard upon the foes of their summoner.
Right click the center Overgrown Roots with an Animation Core.
The creature can be healed by right-clicking on them with Bone Meals.
Smaller than their larger counterparts, these miniature ghasts are unable to spew giant lava bombs, but instead spew small fireballs like Blazes.
These giant, yet fragile, beings float around their summoner, belching forth lava bombs and face their targets properly unlike their natural straight looking counterparts.
A tiny little golem that not only run around in excitement, but also rip through foes with their stone maw.
One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/geomancy/ministrous_focus)Ministrous Focus$(). They can be healed by right-clicking on them with Stone.
Summoned while wearing a $(l:crafts/garment/geo_robe)Geo Robes$() or through ritual, these ministrosities are stronger than their stone counterparts and are immune to fire.
While phantoms usually appear to hunt the sleep-deprived, you've nonetheless found a way to bind these creatures into your service.

When summoned while wearing a Necro Cape, the resulting phantom would appear translucent and gain the ability to pass through blocks! One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/phantasm_focus)Phantasm Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
These thick, sentient vines can block the paths of any creature that attempts to go through.
When summoned or planted underwater, instead of growing into vines, they grow into aquatic kelp instead.
Monstrous and poisonous, these floral creatures shoot poisonous quills towards their master's foes.
Much like their simple cousins, summoning these poisonous plants underwater will spawn an aquatic variant, though unlike their landlubber counterparts, their quills are unaffected by water.
These plants can be healed using Bone Meal on them. If they're already fully healed, they have a chance of generating a new seed instead.
These spectres are called and bound by your will to the point where their scythes won't cut either you or your allies.
One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/reaping_focus)Reaping Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Reapers can be healed by right-clicking on them with Ectoplasm.
Using an $(l:crafts/cores)Animation Core$(), you're able to animate a Block of Redstone into a loyal servant. The Cube is immune to flames and lava and will headbutt any foes it detects.

There's also another feature of the cube that makes it immensely helpful for mining. Shift-right clicking on them with an ore, metal or pickaxe-able blocks will cause them register it, which will cause them to start glowing yellow the closer they are to that specific block. Shift-right click on them with an empty hand to unregister their block.

Plundering through old architectures, you've came across a sort of blueprint for a powerful Golem that's used for wars in ancient days. The Golem seems mighty, though it requires a mold made of Diamonds and Stone Bricks to create such a terrible beast.
Right click the center Redstone Block with an Animation Core.

The Stone Bricks can be substituted with other similar blocks such as Deepslate Bricks. The resulting Golem proves far superior to the Iron Golems as not only is it stronger, but it can be commanded to follow, wander or stay in position through a wand/staff. They can be repaired by right-clicking on them with Redstone Dusts or Blocks.
Diamonds and stones are used to create a powerful mold.

Should the Golem fell from battle or command, they will drop their 'skull'. The Skull can be used to revive the Golem in a cheaper manner. However, the Skull remembers it's original creator and master and the revived Golem will only follow their commands.
Redstone Golems can be part of a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)raiding party$(), though they cannot be leaders.

In ancient times, a monarch had fashioned a powerful weapon, more stronger and terrifying than the Redstone Golems, with guidance of an outside force, before banishing it for unknown reasons. However, the creation process was recorded, perhaps in secret, allowing you to replicate this terrifying monstrosity.
Right click the center Reinforced Redstone Block with an Animation Core.

The Stone Bricks can be substituted with other similar blocks such as Deepslate Bricks for the mold. The Monstrosity is perhaps one of the strongest beings you have created, its power unmatched by other servants. They can be repaired by right-clicking on them with Redstone Blocks.

Should the Monstrosity fell from battle or command, they will drop their head. The Head can be used to revive the Monstrosity in a cheaper manner. However, the Head remembers it's original creator and master and the revived Monstrosity will only follow their commands.
Redstone Monstrosities can be part of a $(l:goety:mutations/illager_servants)raiding party$(), though they cannot be leaders.
Skeletons are slightly more intelligent and quicker than their rotting cousins, but are otherwise still basic in their functions.
The following texts will detail the variants of skeletons a necromancer can summon.
One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/osseous_focus)Osseous Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Skeleton Servants will attempt to kill anyone who hurts you or any hostile creatures nearby. If summoned when the summoner wears a Necro Cape, their arrows pass through allied mobs.
Attempting to summon a Skeleton Servant in a cold tundra exposed to the skies, or summon using a $(l:crafts/frost_staff)Frost Staff$(), will yield a Stray Servant instead.

While being in a Jungle biome, one might have a chance of summoning a Mossy Skeleton Servant instead, a 100%% if summoned with a $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$(). Their arrows inflicts Poison, but if their summoner dons the $(l:crafts/garment/wild_robe)Wild Robes$(), they will inflict Acid Venom.
Under the sea, not only do Skeletons swim, but also wield harpoon shooting crossbows that fly through water better than regular arrows.

Being exposed to an open thunderstorm will have a chance of summoning a Rattled Servant instead, a 100%% if summoned with a $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$(). Their arrows inflicts Spasms, and they are have damage resistance to shock or lightning attacks.
Casting the spell at a Pillager Outpost will summon forth a loyal Skeleton Pillager, which has more health than regular Skeletons and wields a crossbow.
Skeleton Servants can accept any Armor but only Swords/Bows meaning they can either be range or melee attackers.

Curiously, the spell cannot call forth a loyal Wither Skeleton when cast within a Nether Fortress. The charred skeletons seems to hold great magical power and a great loyalty towards their home to be summoned frivolously...
After much research, you've found a way to call forth a former inhabitant of the Fortress, and bind it to your will. They inflict Wither on melee and shoot fire arrows when given a bow.

With an $(l:crafts/cores)Animation Core$() on a Block of Slime or casting Slimy spell, you're able to conjure a loyal Slime Servant. Using a Slimeball will heal them but a Block of Slime on them will not only heal, but also increase their size up to a point.

If a Block of Slime is surrounded by water, the resulting slime appears to be tropical to say the least, with fishes swimming within itself and being able to traverse through water far better than their other variants. When slain, creatures nearby will gain oxygen with the range and amount depending on size.

Slimes aren't the only thing you can animate into loyal servants. Using an animation core on a magma block will transform it into a loyal Magma Cube servant. Instead of a Block of Slime, Magma Cream is used to heal and Magma Blocks to increase their size.
Using an $(l:crafts/cores)Animation Core$() on a Block of Slime or casting Slimy spell while within a Crypt will summon forth a loyal ectoplasmic Crypt Slime.
While piranhas are, in reality, passive and shy creatures, these horrid creatures live up to their vicious and aggressive reputation.

One can call upon a loyal snapper through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting Focus$() underwater or through $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Right-clicking on a loyal Snapper with meat will heal them.
Simple, yet ravenous creatures, these giant arthopods can be great assets in combat, though they are very blind when within bright light.
The following texts will detail the variants of spiders a Spider Nest can train.
The basic Spider found in the dark, only loyal towards you. Does whatever a Spider a can.
A smaller and venomous subspecies of Spiders. Wearing Wild Robes will make these spiders inflict Acid Venom instead of regular Poison.

Unlike their brutish counterparts, Web Spiders would not immediately attack their foes, but instead shoot a ball of web that, when hit, entangles them for a while, where upon they will rush towards them at high speed.
These freezing cold arachnids slows down their target with every bite, and can walk on Powdered Snow with no problems. If their owner wears a Frost Robe, their bites freezes their target instead.
A bone covered spider that shoots Bone Shards at their foes from afar, only going onto melee if their target is close.
Each loyal spider can be healed by right-clicking on them with a piece of meat.

You have of tales of lights dancing in bogs or swamps, luring travellers to their deaths. At first, you thought they would simply lure victims around in circles until they get tired and starve to death. Turns out, instead of having them starve, they would just zap them to death.

The shrines on the peaks seems to hold a copy of a blueprint on making wind-powered golems. Indeed, these golems seems far different from others of its kind, as it appears to require outside energy to function.
Right click the center Jade Block with an Animation Core.

When created the golem will be inactive, immobile and somehow unable to be harmed. The golem requires power from a block called a $(l:goety:crafts/artifice/resonance_crystal)Resonance Crystal$() to function.

To activate the golem, one should register the golem by left-clicking the crystal on it. Once registered, the $(l:goety:crafts/artifice/resonance_crystal)crystal$() must then be powered by a Wind Blower, blowing wind on it.

When powered, the crystal will activate the golem. Should the crystal be broken or deactivated, the golem will shut down and be inactive once more.$(br2)The golem can only Follow or Stand By, it cannot Wander like other servants. If damaged, the golem can be repaired using Jade or Jade Blocks.
When deactivated, right-clicking on the golem with an empty hand will rotate them towards you at an angle.
A simple yet powerful ritual that conjures up a Thunderstorm. Useful to those who wish to hide from the sun.
Dark colored and vicious counterparts of regular goats, these dark omens will ram onto their masters enemies or skewer them with their horns, or bites if they lose them.

One can call upon twilight goats through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/hunting_focus)Hunting Focus$() while on a mountain, or through casting it with a $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Right-clicking on a loyal Twilight Goat with any type of edible food will heal them.

These ancient warriors have once served a necromancer that had stolen a piece of dark magic. Their glaives can reach further than most swords and can damage multiple foes in front of them. Their shields might break after a single hit, but it will absorbed that hit completely.

If they're shield-less, right click on them with any Wooden Planks to give them their shield back when they're not attacking.$(br)One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/vanguard_focus)Vanguard Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Your own group of Vexes. These Vexes pretty much acts the same as Evoker Vexes, only they will follow you and attack on your behalf.
Unlike other fleshier Servants, Vexes will not wander and stop following you and will not accept weapons/armor as they're too big for them.

Wartlings have the same properties as Spiders, though they are much smaller and weaker. A Wartling can only exist for 9 seconds before either dying or returning back to its user, where it will disappear and heal the user the amount of health it had.

Should the user have a negative effect on them, the next Wartling will take and 'store' that effect in them, which will cause them to leave a cloud of the stored effect once they perish. The stored effect does not effect them and they cannot be effected by the same effect as the one they stored. These Wartlings do not return to their user.

Despite their names, Whisperers are loud and odd creatures that can conjure forth quick growing vines to block their target's path, summon two Poison-Quill Vines and entangling roots upon their target's legs.

One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/wild/whispering_focus)Whispering Focus$(), or by right-clicking on the center Jungle Leaves of this configuration with an Animation Core for one without limited lifespan.
Right click the Moss Block with an Animation Core.
The creature can be healed by right-clicking on them with Bone Meals.
These spectres are called and bound by your will to the point where their own Ice Bouquets do not touch either you or your allies.
One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/spooky_focus)Spooky Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Wraiths can be healed by right-clicking on them with Ectoplasm.
A variant of the wraith, these acid gas calling phantasms are called when summoned within a Swamp biome.
A variant of the wraith, these ice puking creatures are called when summoned within a $(l:world/crypts)Crypt$().
Zombies are the most common undead creature to crawl out of the dark, and it's no surprise that summoning and controlling them aren't exactly hard to do, whether it be from spell or ritual.
The following texts will detail the variants of zombies a necromancer can summon.
One can call these creatures through the use of a $(l:focuses/necromancy/rotting_focus)Rotting Focus$(), or through a ritual which summons one without a limited lifespan.
Zombie Servants are simple in their functions, kill anyone who hurts you or any hostile creatures and follow you much like Tamed Wolves, only taller and stinkier.
Zombie Servants can be summoned or converted into different variants. Casting the Rotting Focus in a Desert exposed to the sky will summon a Husk Servant.
Trying to summon a Zombie underwater would summon a Drowned Servant instead. Drowned Servants can accept Tridents and will attack the same way as a regular Drowned.
A simple Zombie Villager, only more loyal and less curable. Summoning a zombie in a Village will summon a Zombie Villager Servant.

Summoning a Zombie in a cold, snowy environment, or with a $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$(), will call forth a Frozen Zombie Servant. Frozen Zombie Servants will slow down their targets through their fists or their snowballs they chuck. Much like Strays, they don't take damage from Freezing.

While being in a Jungle biome, one might have a chance of summoning a Jungle Zombie Servant instead, a 100%% if summoned with a $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$(). Their attacks inflicts Poison, but if their summoner dons the $(l:crafts/garment/wild_robe)Wild Robes$(), they will inflict Acid Venom.

When exposed to an open thunderstorm, there's a 50%% chance of summoning a Frayed Servant instead of a regular Zombie, a 100%% when summoned with a $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$(). They inflict Spasms when they attack and take 50%% less damage from shock or lightning attacks.
Summoning a zombie within the mansions of the Illagers, will summon forth loyal Zombie Vindicators instead. It appears that many Vindicators are buried within their homes, still clutching their axes.

The Nether is full of Zombified Piglins that it comes to no surprised that casting the spell within the abominable realm will call forth one that's loyal towards you. Fire-resistant and scares Piglins like any other of its kind.

The Brutish guardians of the bastions rarely, if ever, leave their home, and most have their bodies burnt by the surrounding lava. Nonetheless, there's still a chance of summoning a Zombified version when casting within their holds.
Zombie Servants in all variants can accept any Armor but only accept Swords or Axes.
With the power of souls, you've conjured a rain of arrows upon a location or a target.
Summons a row of magical Fangs in front of you that deals damage that ignores the targets' armor(Unless it's enchanted). When crouching, a circles of Fangs are summoned around you.
The focus will initially summon four magical shields to orbit around you, each absorbing an attack before breaking, knocking back the attacker. After a while, the shields will disappear.

The command focus allows the caster to command a servant to move towards a position. If used on a creature, it will move to the creature's location, but if the creature is a mount, most servants can ride on it.

To use the command focus, it must be equipped in a wand/staff. Then the caster must left click the wand/staff on a servant to start commanding it. The caster can shift-right click into the air to remove the servant from the command focus.
The servant can still move, even if it's on Standing By mode. To dismount a mounted servant, shift-right click on the mount itself.
The Night Beacon holds tremendous power, you believe that by supplying it with Soul Energy, you'll be be able to transform it's night bringing beam into something more devastating!
Sometimes one forgets, or is unable to place, their crafting table, so having one on the go makes crafting more convenient!

With the power of Ender Pearls and the Hunger Core, you are able to call upon Fangs at the bottom of any creature around you. More accurate than the average Biting Focus, though only if said creature doesn't move.

Focuses have their own specialize enchantments, but not all Focuses can be enchanted nor accept every enchantments. There are many enchantments that are only applicable to certain Focuses. Enchanted Focuses doubles the amount of Soul Energy needed to cast.
Potency increases the damage of your spells.
pages.title: Potency

pages.text: Your spells and your summons lasts longer.
pages.title: Duration

pages.text: Increases the radius of your spells, this generally means any explosive spells has a higher explosive radius. For certain spells, radius allows spells to more accurately find the nearest enemy to hit.
pages.title: Radius

pages.text: Your spells sets targets on fire or extends how long the target remains burning.
pages.title: Burning

pages.text: Your spells goes further by 2 blocks per level. The most common of enchantments.
pages.title: Range

pages.text: Your spells absorb health from targets when hit. Very Rare and is not compatible with Potency.
pages.title: Life Absorb

pages.text: Your spells immediately pulls blocks broken by them into your inventory. Very Rare.
pages.title: Magnetize

pages.text: Projectiles made from your spells move quicker.
pages.title: Velocity

pages.text: With this spell, right-clicking on a block or a target directly will set them aflame, simple as that.

Studying Illusion magics allows you to craft a Focus that will conjure several doppelgangers that will distract hostile creatures from attacking you. The doppelgangers do no damage whatsoever... unless one wears a full set of Illusive Robes, though their damage output won't be too substantial.
The focus strengthens your skin against physical attacks, temporarily increasing your armor points.
This focus allows you to shoot a bolt that Curses targets and produce a noxious ground of black magic.
A modified Command Focus that can stores up to 8 servants for you to command with.
Casting with this focus causes an explosion of Soul Energy at your position, hurting all nearby creatures and launching them away. The explosion deals magic damage and does not harm the caster.

Summons a row of royal, magical, spikes in front of you that constantly deals damage, which ignores armor (Unless it's enchanted), to any targets caught in them. When crouching, a circles of Spikes are summoned around you.
With the power of the Ruby, you've managed to replicate the power of the Warden's Sonic Boom, allowing you to use its ability against others!
With this focus, you're capable of rapidly fire bolts of Soul Energy towards your foe, dealing knockback and magic damage.
Casting this spell with a $(l:crafts/staff/nameless_staff)Nameless Staff$() will shoot forth Necro Bolts, which does far more damage and can hit multiple targets, instead.
This focus allows you to heal wounds through soul energy. However, the healing amount is not consistent, having a chance of healing a large portion or a little.

You are able to make a magical light source by shooting a bolt of Soul Energy on a Block. At first, the light isn't as strong as a Torch, but it does drive Piglins away, but with some glowstone and netherrack, your light shines brighter. It also illuminates a creature if it's hit by it.

While throwing light around is well and good, there are times where you wish to light up entire caverns and rooms. With this focus, you're able to summon glow lights, and replace soul lights with them, around the area as you cast.

Much like the Envioker and Vizier, you are able to shoot out a copy of your sword towards wherever you're looking at. You must have a Sword on either your main hand or off hand to cast this spell. Casting this spell uses up your Sword's durability. The Focus can be enchanted with Velocity which will increase the speed of the flying sword.

Summons a mighty tooth above a location, a target or the caster, if shifting, that crashes to the ground and summons pikes around it, causing creatures to fly up in the air and be slowed massively for 5 seconds.
Causes a targeted item or creature to float towards the caster's crosshairs, but only if the target is equal or smaller than the caster's size, if the focus is not enchanted with Potency.

Through the old Bestiary and some notes on the Allays, you've found the necessary ingredients to summon/create your own Vexes. Strangely, the Bestiary mentions of Demons and Imps in the Nether. Curious...
This spell lets loose a menacing hum that weakens non-allied creatures in a large area around the caster, decreasing their damage and their defenses.
Inspired by the vanguards, you've devised a way to summon and armed powerful, but slow, zombies with heavy armor and mace.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more blackguards at once.
The flames of the dead can be quite chilling. With ectoplasms, you've managed to summon forth the cold flames of the dead on a location or at your foe's feet.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more icy flames in a 3x3 grid instead of 2x2.

The spell deals an amount of damage equal to the target's current health, but also deals 125%% of it upon the caster. If the caster has enough health to survive, the target will take the full damage, otherwise it will deal as much damage upon both the target and the caster as possible without killing the latter.

Taking the life out of your enemies is one thing, but actually eating it is another. The spell siphons a non-allied target the caster's looking at, hurting them and healing the caster the amount the target lost.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() will give Weakness effect to target.
Skeletons can be quite annoying to those who lack the patience to carry a Shield. Now you have the power to summon and command one to turn others into pincushions.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more skeletons at once.
Phantoms are quite an oddity, beings that fly between reality and un-reality, only appearing towards the sleep-deprived. With this focus, you're able to summon and bind them to your will.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more phantoms at once.
These soul hungering apparitions are not only useful at mowing down multiple foes, but also gather soul energy for their necromantic master.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more reapers at once.

The true first step to Necroturgy is to summon and command a Zombie. Zombies comes in multiple variants, and the focus allows you to summon a variant depending on location and environment where the spell is casted.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more zombies at once.
With this focus, you're able to summon forth Skulls haunted by spirits from beyond that will follow you and charge at any nearby hostile mob, exploding on impact.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more skulls at once.
Wraiths aren't exactly the most common of undead creatures, only in recent times do they start appearing. With some Spirit Fabrics, you're able to summon and bound one to your command.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more wraiths at once.
You've discovered a way to summon loyal guards from beyond the grave using this focus. You have a feeling that this spell was stolen and repurposed from an ancient king.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() summons more vanguards at once.
The spell covers you with electricity and propels you, like a riptide enchanted trident, towards where you're looking at, shocking any non-allied creatures along the way.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() increases AoE, chance of inflicting Spasms and deal chain lightning effect.

A spell that requires the caster to directly right click a living target. When doing so, the target will become Charged and will gain a charge when casted again. Level 1 Charged makes the target move and deal damage 10%% more. Level 2 Charged makes the target move 25%% faster, but deal 25%% less damage. Adding another level causes the target to take damage and lose all charges.
Added from pvzfan's suggestion
You let loose an explosion of electricity at your position, hurting all nearby creatures and shocking them. The explosion deals shock damage and does not harm the caster.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() increases chance of inflicting Spasms and deal chain lightning effect.
The spell shoots a ball of electricity that, when casted looking at a valid entity, follows their target before hitting them or any solid object.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() shoots electro orbs that have a higher chance of inflicting Spasms and electrically explode, dealing damage to multiple targets.

Finally, with this focus in your hands, you can now summon the fury of the heavens on a foe or a location! When not casted from $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$(), the summoned lightning will be affected by Lightning Rods.
Summons a storm cloud high above a target block or creature, where it will rain and periodically shoots thunderbolts to any nearby non-allied creature.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() increases the size of the clouds and cause its thunderbolts to deal chain lightning.

The power of electricity shoots out from you, shocking any creature in front of you. When not casted from $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$(), the electricity will go towards the closest Lightning Rod.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() will also deal a chain lightning effect and have an increased chance of inflicting Spasms effect.
With some ingredients and magic, you're able to summon Sprites to fly around and attack your foes with tiny lightning bolts.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() summon more Sprites.
The spell sacrifices the size of the Electro Orbs to allow the caster to rapidly shoot smaller orbs that can arc towards a target the caster is looking at after charging up.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() will cause your bolts to have a higher chance of inflicting Spasms and have minor chain lightning effect.

Instead of multiple electric sparks, you shoot one big spark that deals more damage. When not casted from $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$(), the thunderbolt will be affected by Lightning Rods.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() will also deal a chain lightning effect and have an increased chance of inflicting Spasms effect.
The focus allows you to cover the landscape with lightning bolts from the heavens.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/storm_staff)Storm Staff$() summon more lightning.
Infusing the Arrow Rain Focus with the power of frost, you call upon a rain of ice spikes instead of arrows.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will rain ice spears, larger and piercing version of ice spikes, instead.

The focus not only increases your armor points, but it also cause any being that attacks you in melee to freeze. The spell can also be casted onto an allied creature by looking at them while crouch casting.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will apply the effect to nearby allies around the caster or the target.
With a cold breath, creatures in front of you will shiver to the grave.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will not only increases the damage, but also snows and freezes terrain.

You unleash an explosion of frost at your position, or at a target's position while crouching, hurting all nearby creatures and freezing them. The explosion deals freeze damage and does not harm the caster.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will increase explosion radius a bit and cause targets to freeze a bit faster.
The spell summons forth an $(l:summons/ice_golems)Ice Golem$(), a powerful servant that's resistant to freeze damage and can rarely summon an explosion of frost..
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will have a chance of summoning an additional golem.
Summons a cloud of snow high above a target block or creature, where it will rain freezing snow, that deals small damage and gives Freezing for 5 seconds.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will cause the hail cloud to follow a valid target.
Shoots a spike of ice towards the caster's line of sight. Creatures struck by the spike will get Freezing from 1 to 3 seconds.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will shoot an Ice Spear, a larger variant that pierces through enemies, instead.
This spell summons forth a ball of frost that slowly pass through objects, freezing and damaging nearby creatures. The ball increases in size as it goes.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() increases the Ice Storm's initial size.

You have learned a branch of Illager Magic called Iceology. With this focus, you are able to summon a chunk of floating ice above a target that will then smash onto them after a small amount of time, stunning them for a few seconds.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/frost_staff)Frost Staff$() will decrease hovering time for Ice Chunks.
Conjures a cloud that negates all fall damage when a creature falls on it. The cloud will automatically position itself to the ground.

The focus sends forth a powerful cyclone pulling in any nearby creatures and throwing them around. Casting with the $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() will cause the cyclone to constantly deal a small amount of damage to targets caught in it.
With the power of the graceful dragon and control of the Elytra, you've managed refine the Launching Focus to let you properly fly through your wand or staff(by holding down right mouse button).
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() will make you fly faster.
After some tinkering and experimentation, you've managed to create a spell that propels you into the air, allowing you to fly in a crude yet effective manner.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() launches you further.
The focus hones the wind into a thin, sharp blade, shooting out to slice any non-allied creature in its path at high speed.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() increases the initial width of the blade.
The spell emits a circular wind blast around the caster, pushing back non-allied creatures a certain distance away, and slowing them down briefly.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() increases the area of effect.
The Focus allows you to summon a powerful gust of air at a location or at the feet of creatures that will, after a second, throw them into air, damaging them.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() increases the area of effect.

This focus allows the user to surround themselves with a barrier of wind which pushes back all nearby creatures and potentially deflects projectiles. The powerful winds created by this spell also allows the caster to hover in place as it is cast. When cast with the $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$(), the winds will deflect projectiles more efficiently and the caster floats even higher.

The Wind Blast Focus allows you to summon a blast of wind in front of you, knocking back creatures in your line of sight. The blast deals no damage unfortunately, but you can throw creatures off of ledges from a, admittedly short, distance!
When cast by different staffs, the wind blast might give additional effects to targets.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$() increases knockback distance.
A spell that requires the caster to directly right click a living target, where upon the target is teleported away from the caster. Perfect for getting rid of certain foes or annoyances!
Despite the name, the focus doesn't blast anything. However, it does summon forth $(l:summons/enderling_servants#blastling)creatures that blasts volleys of hard hitting goop$().
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() summons more blastlings at once.
This focus allows you to teleport towards a location you are looking at, provided said location is within range.

While certain focuses can summon all associated servants towards you, certain servants don't have that and/or you want to summon a specific servant. The Call Focus allows you to do just that. Simply left click on the servant and it will save it, allowing you to summon them when casting with it. To remove the save, just right click the air with it while crouching.

The focus taps into the energies of the End, granting you true invisibility that hides even your armor for a small duration. However, interacting with any creature or block will not only break the invisibility, but also teleports you back to where you cast the spell.
A simple focus, that when cast allows you to access your Ender Chest from the tip of your wand.

The Recall Focus allows the caster to teleport back to a location saved by the Focus. To use the Focus, it needs to have a location saved by right-clicking on either an $(l:crafts/artifice/arca)Arca$() owned by the Caster, a Bed, or a Respawn Anchor with it. Shift-right clicking the Focus will clear any saved location.
The spell also allows the caster to teleport their servant to the stored location, where they will stand by if they are able, by right-clicking on them.

With enough soul energy, the focus opens up a rift within the world into the very void, sucking in all nearby non-allied creatures towards it, damaging them when sucked in, before closing in a massive explosion.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() will cause the rift explosion apply Void Touched effect.

The focus feels gooey by touch, but it does not seem to secrete any goo whatsoever. The same cannot be said to the creature it can summon, $(l:summons/enderling_servants#snareling)a gangly caricature of humanity with long arms, a jaw on its chest and a glowing back-sac$().
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() summons more snarelings at once.

The echoes of the void allows you to create a spell that, when concentrated, continuously summon projectiles that, after a second of being conjured, will home onto a foes location and explode in a blast of void energy.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() summons more projectiles.
A modified Call Focus that, rather than storing an individual servant, stores the servant's species and type, allowing you to call all servants of that type instead.
Using this focus on a wall or floor will create an ethereal tunnel leading to the other side. Tunnels will only open for a short amount of time and cannot open through certain blocks.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() increases the tunnel size from 3x3 to 5x5.
Instead of continuously summoning several projectiles, this spell shoots a massive ball of void energy that will explode into magical flames and shoot out several homing balls of void at nearby foes.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() summons more projectiles.
You feel this focus gazing back at you. With it, you'll summon forth a creature of the End, a $(l:summons/enderling_servants#watchling)grotesque humanoid mass of eyes and darkness$().
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/void_staff)Void Staff$() summons more watchlings at once.

While there's some mystery on the Blazes' rebellion, even after learning the methods of their creation, you've managed to create a focus that summons one that doesn't have a rebellious rod on their body.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() summons more blazes at once.
An upgraded version of the humble Fireball spell. Now, you can shoot a barrage of fireballs and fly up like the Blazes.
Enchanting the focus with Duration will increase the number of volleys that you can shoot.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will cause you to shoot two more fireballs per volley.
You emit an fiery explosion at your position, hurting all nearby creatures and burning them. The explosion deals fire damage and does not harm the caster or their allies.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() increases explosion range a bit.
Like a mythic Red Dragons of old, you breath flames out in front of you, burning any creature in its path.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will not only increases the damage, but also sets fire to terrain.
The power of the Blazes are now at your finger tip. No longer will you need to use a Dispenser and Fire Charges, now you can be the Dispenser!
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will shoot two extra fireballs.
The power of the Nether allows you to summon forth pillars of flames that either surrounds you or, if looking directly at a valid target, your foe.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will double the radius of fire pillars.
The focus allows you to summon forth miniature Ghasts that, while less destructive, are still potent fire spewers.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() summons more ghasts at once.
Wearing a Nether Robes will casting this spell will summon forth Ghast Servants instead of Mini-Ghasts, though in smaller amounts even when cast with Nether Staff.
The Hogging focus summons an short-lived ethereal hoglin that will charge towards an enemy and explode upon contact.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() summons more Burning Hoglins at once.
You can feel the power of the Nether overtaking you. Unlike the Ghasts, you do not weep. After all, it is a good pain. Your Lavaballs deal no environmental damage when cast while crouching.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will shoot two extra lava bombs.

Ancient villager legends speaks of giant hoglin-like creatures that shoot Magma Cubes at their foes, leaving devastation. Inspired and with some tinkering, you've made a focus that shoots out a ball of magma that leaves an explosion... and a couple of loyal Magma Cubes at the site of impact.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() increases explosion range.
Infusing the Arrow Rain Focus with the power of the nether, you call upon a rain of explosive lava bombs instead of arrows.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() increases the number of lava bombs falling from the sky.
The unholy blood of the Nether's emissary allows you to upgrade your Skull Focus to replicate the skulls of the Wither! Beware of its destructive abilities!
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() shoots two more wither skulls.

With the power of the focus, you're able to harass your enemies by either summoning either a row, square or randomly placed Totemic Walls in front of them, or, if crouching while spell casting, summon either a singular or multiple Totemic Bombs around them. If not crouching, always summons a row of Totemic Walls if not targeting an enemy.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() increases chance of summoning four Totemic Bombs instead of one.
The focus shoots a beam of magical energy that's capable of mining the very rock and stone with tougher materials taking longer to mine.
The Potency enchantment increases the speed of mining and on higher levels allows the spell to mine blocks that require diamond or netherite tools.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() will cause the spell to mine in a 3x3 area, so long as the blocks are mine-able with pickaxe or shovel.
The focus conjures a fist from the earth beneath a target or a position, dealing damage to non-allied entities and punching them up in the air.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() will conjure multiple fists to nearby enemies.
The focus allows you to summon forth a small volcano that would spew several pyroclastic rocks to the sky, which would fall around it, exploding and hopefully hurting and stunning your foes.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() summon three small volcanoes instead of one.
The spell summons a $(l:summons/ministrosities)Stone Ministrosity$(), a simple golem that can move quickly to bite down your foes.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() will summon additional Ministrosities. Casting while wearing $(l:crafts/garment/geo_robe)Geo Robes$() will summon Redstone Ministrosities instead.
Equipping this focus on a wand or staff allows you to pulverize certain blocks into cracked versions, or into gravel and then to sand, by right-clicking on a block.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() will pulverize 3x3 blocks un-enchanted.
The caster summons forth tremors in front of them, hurting and flinging non-allied creatures towards the air. Casting the spell while crouching will summon tremors around the caster instead.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() will summon tremors in an arc angle that will also disable shields. Cast crouching increases radius.
A simple focus that rotates and changed a block's orientation and facing direction.
The focus conjures up mines around the caster, where they will prime after a second and explode, non-destructively, when a non-allied target steps near them.

Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() changes how the spell is cast. Instead of, by default, instantly summoning three scatter mines, the caster must continuously cast the spell until up to fourteen mines has spawned around them.
The focus grants you Tremor Sense, which causes any creature that's on the ground to appear as though they're glowing for you. The effect only works if you're also standing on the ground.
The Potency enchantment increases the effect level of Tremor Sense, doubling the radius per level.

Ever heard of the phrase 'killing two birds with one stone'? While these stones are to fragile to hit more than one target, it not only causes the target to have a hard time jumping or flying, but it also deals more damage to them if they're not on the ground.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() shoots three stones instead of one.
This spell lets loose a shockwave that knocks back foes and stunning them for a few seconds. The spell's radius is increased if the caster on the ground.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/geo_staff)Geo Staff$() increases the radius a bit.
The focus allows you to summon biomines, which are egg-like structures that explode into poisonous gas when popped or if an non-allied creature is nearby.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() will summon forth more biomines.

An odd spell that summons forth a bubble that bounces from surfaces and creatures, somehow hurting them as though it were sharp or made of acid. After bouncing multiple times, the bubble will burst, hurting nearby non-allied creatures.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() will summon multiple Bouncy Bubbles instead of one.
Somehow, you're able to create a spell that summons forth and binds the guardians of the monuments under your command.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() will summon two guardians at once.

The spell replicates the power of the Ocean Monument's Guardians whereupon it projects a laser towards any non-allied creature you're directly looking it that will damage them after a while. Unfortunately, much like the Guardians, the laser will stop once direct sight is broken.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() increases the spell's base damage by one heart.
The spell allows you to shoot a torrent of hot steaming missiles towards the direction you're looking at, damaging and knocking back creatures when hit.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() allows the caster to shoot more torrents of missiles.
The spell conjures a surge of flowing water in front of the caster, pushing back and damaging non-allied targets.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() will summon three tidal surges in front of the caster instead of one.
The powers of the deep allows you to conjure tridents to fall around you, blasting your foes away with channeled lightning bolts.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() summon more tridents around you with more elaborate patterns.
The focus shoots out a high-pressure stream of water that will wash away any foes, especially ones sensitive to water. It can also put out fires.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() will cause stream to apply Sapped.
The spell conjures a powerful tentacle from the caster's hand, whipping foes in front of them, though only in a small range.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() summons another tentacle after the initial tentacle hits a target.
Based on @rangoonruler's suggestion
The spell lobs an thorny ball of wild energies that will grow several poisonous thorns around the area of its impact.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() increases the radius.

Through rotten flesh, you're able to enlarge and engorge some of the flies summoned with the $(l:focuses/wild/swarm_focus)Swarm Focus$() into $(l:summons/carrion_flies)Carrion Flies$(). When any of them kills their target, maggots will grow from their corpse and will follow you as well.
When cast with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$(), more Carrion Flies are summoned, wearing a Wild Robe will strengthened them, increasing their health and damage.
Added from @NUTTAR's suggestion

This spell will summon entangling roots upon a target. If the roots managed to catch a target in time, they will be unable to move until the roots retreat back into the ground. When cast with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$(), the roots will be summoned underneath 8 nearby non-allied creatures.
Wearing a $(l:crafts/garment/wild_robe)Wild Robe$(), will cause the roots to continuously damage the entrapped target.
This focus allows you to shoot a grappling hook made of vines and thorns that will attach itself to any solid surface it lands on, pulling you along the way.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() allows the hook to shoot further and negates fall damage when attached to a grappling hook.

$(l:summons/black_wolves)Black wolves$() are supernatural, or demonic hounds mentioned in folklore that are said to be seen throughout the Overworld. With the focus, you're able to summon or conjure them for aid. When on top of mountains, you'll summon forth $(l:summons/twilight_goats)twilight goats$(), vicious cousins of regular goats. When underwater, you'll summon forth $(l:summons/snappers)Snappers$(), ferocious piranha-like creatures that will gnaw on your foes.

When cast with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$(), more wolves are summoned, wearing a Wild Robe will strengthened them, where their claws and bites Curses their target. When cast with $(l:crafts/staff/wind_staff)Wind Staff$(), you'll call forth Twilight Goats. When cast with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() you'll summon Snappers... even on land. Snappers will only teleport towards you if crouch-casting underwater.
The spell summons forth an $(l:summons/leapleaves)Leapleaves$(), a powerful servant that can jump high and smash hard upon the foes of their summoner.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() will have a chance of summoning an additional leapleaf.

Bears are strong, but wild and aggressive. With your dark powers, you're able to summon forth bears that are loyal towards you to the very end. When cast with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$(), two bears are summoned at once, wearing a Wild Robe will summoned stronger versions where their claws even inflict Sapped on their victim.
When casting this focus in the Nether, instead of a Bear, you call forth a loyal Hoglin.

With soul energy, you conjure forth powerful immobile vines to block your targets path or, if crouching/shifting, conjure forth a powerful flowered vine that shoots poisonous quills. Shift-casting while looking at a target will cause the poisonous vine to be summoned next to you instead.

Casting the spell underwater will summon powerful immobile kelps instead. No difference other than aesthetic and need to be underwater, though the poisonous kelp's quills aren't affected by water. Wearing a $(l:crafts/garment/wild_robe)Wild Robe$() allows you to move past the vines and kelps.
Shoots a poison quill towards the caster's line of sight. Creatures struck by the quill will be poisoned.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() will shoot a quill that pierces through multiple targets.
Conjures forth loyal $(l:summons/slime_servants)Slime Servant$() around you to do your bidding.

Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() summon more Slime Servants. Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/abyss_staff)Abyss Staff$() will summon Tropical Slimes, $(l:crafts/staff/nether_staff)Nether Staff$() will summon Magma Cubes, $(l:crafts/staff/necro_staff)Necro Staff$() will summon Crypt Slimes.
You conjure and call forth a spew of insects upon your targets, dealing damage that upon death, a loyal swarm of insects will rise from the corpse and independently attack other targets.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() will cause targets to be poisoned.
After researching the Jungle for a while, you've managed to devise a way to call forth its Whisperers as loyal servants. Casting this underwater will call upon the whisperers of the waves instead.
Casting with $(l:crafts/staff/wild_staff)Wild Staff$() will summon an additional whisperer.

pages.text: There are many ways you can augment your brew! A novice should know that adding Redstone increases duration and Glowstone increases power, but there's more to it than that! Much like capacity, the ingredients must be put in order!
